articles.title: Lamar Jackson injury update: Ravens QB ruled out against Bills after suffering thumb injury
articles.summary: Just when Baltimore Ravens fans thought things were finally looking up, Lamar Jackson's return took a scary turn.
articles.body: Just when Baltimore Ravens fans thought things were finally looking up, Lamar Jackson's return took a scary turn. The star quarterback was back on the field after missing three straight games with an ankle injury, but his comeback against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, November 1, lasted just one offensive play. And honestly, it was probably the last thing Ravens fans wanted to see.Lamar Jackson suffers injury on first offensive playJackson was making his return against Josh Allen and the Bills, with Baltimore hoping its two-time MVP could give the struggling offense a much-needed boost. But things went wrong almost immediately. On Baltimore's opening offensive snap, Jackson attempted a pass to wide receiver Zay Flowers. As he released the ball, his right hand collided with Bills pass rusher Gregory Rousseau's arm.Jackson appeared to be in immediate pain after the play. He walked toward the sideline before heading straight to the locker room, leaving fans worried about what had just happened. The Ravens initially listed Jackson as questionable to return with a right thumb injury. However, the team later ruled him out for the remainder of the game.Jackson's return was supposed to be a big moment for Baltimore. The quarterback had missed the previous three games because of an ankle injury, including a difficult stretch for the Ravens, who went 1-2 during his absence.Before getting sidelined, Jackson had started the season strongly, completing 70.8% of his passes for 967 yards, six touchdowns and just one interception in four starts. His return was expected to bring some much-needed energy to an offense that had struggled without him. Instead, Baltimore suddenly found itself facing another quarterback setback.For Ravens fans, the bigger question now is what Jackson's latest injury could mean moving forward. After already missing valuable time with his ankle issue, another setback is certainly not ideal for a team hoping to get its season back on track. For now, the confirmed concern is his right thumb injury, and any longer-term implications will depend on further medical updates. Jackson's return was supposed to be a fresh start. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes once joined Brittany's soccer ambitions as an investor; their $325 million Kansas City Current story has a bigger meaning
articles.summary: Forbes reported in April that the Kansas City Current are worth $325 million, up 18% from last year, second in the NWSL behind Angel City at $340 million.
articles.body: Forbes reported in April that the Kansas City Current are worth $325 million, up 18% from last year, second in the NWSL behind Angel City at $340 million. Brittany Mahomes backed the club early. Patrick Mahomes became a co-owner in January 2023, alongside Angie and Chris Long. Few people expected a women's soccer team in Kansas City to climb this fast. The valuation is a paper number, but it shows what a club can build when it owns its stadium and fills it every week.How the Mahomes investment reached $325 millionA year ago, Forbes valued the Current at $275 million, so the club added roughly $50 million in twelve months. Angel City still leads on value. On revenue, though, the Current were ahead in 2024. Forbes had them at $36 million against $35 million for Angel City.Brittany was in the picture before the first match. Patrick arrived later, after buying into the Royals and Sporting Kansas City. He also holds a stake in the Alpine F1 team.The Current are different from those holdings. This one began as her project, and he followed.Why the Current make money when others struggleFans are the simple part of the answer. Kansas City sold out every regular-season home game in one recent season, and revenue rose by more than $20 million. A sold-out stadium sells tickets, but it also sells sponsorships and stronger media deals.The league's structure helps too. One analysis of the club points out that the Current operate inside a closed system with controlled spending, centralized growth and expanding media value. There is no relegation. Salaries have limits. An owner can plan five years ahead without worrying that one bad season wipes out the investment.That is why the story is bigger than two famous names. Celebrity gets attention. Stable rules and a building the club controls are what make investors believe a number like $325 million.What the stadium plans say about the next phaseOwnership is already pushing for more. The city council approved a financing framework worth up to $185 million for a CPKC Stadium expansion and the wider Berkley Riverfront project. Front Office Sports reported that the whole development is forecast to exceed $800 million. Public money is part of that mix, so expect more debate over how much help a private club should get from the city.The ownership group is also thinking beyond soccer. Mahomes and the Current's owners pitched the WNBA on an expansion team, using the club's growth as their main argument.It is worth remembering that nobody has sold anything. The $325 million figure is an estimate. It only becomes real money if someone buys the club at that price, and the Mahomeses have shown no sign they want to sell.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Vikings coach sends message after Lions’ Jack Campbell suffers scary injury
articles.summary: The linebacker left the field on a stretcher after colliding with a teammate trying to make a tackle.
articles.body:
Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell sent a heartfelt message to Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell, who was carted off the field with a scary injury in their game Sunday, Nov. 1.

The Lions' Pro Bowl linebacker was taken off the field on a stretcher during the Week 8 game after he was hurt while trying to tackle T.J. Hockenson.

"We're all thinking and praying for Jack Campbell," O'Connell said after the game. "I asked Dan after the game if he had any update. He didn't have much of one, but it's definitely something that you hate seeing.

"Still hard to talk about the result when you see something like that."

Campbell and defensive end Eric O'Neill both hit Hockenson at the same time and Campbell appeared to get bent backwards as he fell to the ground. Campbell was motionless on the field as he was attended to.

In his own postgame remarks, the Lions' head coach, Dan Campbell, said Jack Campbell "is being taken care of. We don't have any new information. We'll keep you updated as this goes." MORE: Former Raiders running back, Super Bowl champion, dies

Another Lions linebacker, Derrick Barnes, was also unaware of his teammate's condition when he spoke to reporters after the game.

"I don't know even know what's going on, but I'm going to be there to support him," Barnes said. "When you see your brother go down like that, there's a fire that gets lit … that says it's time to go, really."

articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have another reason to be excited about Kansas City's sporting future.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have another reason to be excited about Kansas City's sporting future. The couple, who are part of the Kansas City Current's ownership group, are backing a club with ambitions that stretch far beyond the football pitch. In June 2026, the NWSL side unveiled ambitious renderings of an expanded CPKC Stadium and a major riverfront development. The proposal could transform the area into a major destination for sports, entertainment and tourism, while giving women's football an even bigger stage in Kansas City.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes' KC Current target 18,000-seat stadiumThe Kansas City Current's expansion plans represent a major step in the club's long-term vision. The renderings, presented during a Kansas City City Council committee meeting on June 30, showed how CPKC Stadium could evolve from its existing 11,500-seat capacity into an 18,000-seat venue.That would add 6,500 seats, giving the club more room to welcome supporters and potentially host larger sporting events. The proposal also includes a parking garage, mixed-use buildings, improved infrastructure and pedestrian access connecting different parts of the riverfront.The city was considering issuing up to $235 million in special obligation bonds to support the development at the time. The wider project also aims to bring more commercial activity and public spaces to the Berkley Riverfront area.Kansas City Mayor Quinton Lucas welcomed the club's growing influence, highlighting the importance of investment in women's sports.“The Kansas City Current presents one of the greatest success stories in our city’s recent history, and CPKC Stadium has already proven that world-class investment in women’s sports pays off,” Mayor Quinton Lucas said in a news release earlier this month.For Mahomes, the investment also carries personal significance. Patrick joined Brittany in the Current's ownership group in 2023, becoming the first active NFL player to hold equity in an NWSL team. Brittany had already been involved with the club and has a background in professional football.KC Current's riverfront expansion could reshape Kansas City's sporting futureThe stadium is only one part of the larger vision. The Current wants to turn the surrounding riverfront into a place where supporters can spend time beyond matchdays.The ownership group has already invested more than $350 million in private capital along the riverfront and aims to commit more than $1 billion in private investment over the next decade.The club believes the development could attract major events, create jobs and bring more visitors to Kansas City. It could also strengthen the city's chances of hosting international competitions, including the 2031 FIFA Women's World Cup or the 2031 Men's Rugby World Cup.The Current summed up its ambition with a simple message: “Building a place where families and generations can gather, celebrate and connect.”The club has also made its broader philosophy clear, saying it has “always been bigger than a stadium.”For Mahomes and Brittany, the project represents an opportunity to help build something lasting in Kansas City. It is no longer just about creating a successful women's football team. articles.title: Dak Prescott Calls Out Brian Schottenheimer Criticism After Cowboys' Loss vs. Cardinals
articles.summary: Brian Schottenheimer has struggled to put the pieces together since taking over as the Dallas Cowboys' head coach, but quarterback Dak Prescott doesn't think it's fair to put all the blame on him.
articles.body:
Brian Schottenheimer has struggled to put the pieces together since taking over as the Dallas Cowboys' head coach, but quarterback Dak Prescott doesn't think it's fair to put all the blame on him.

After a loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, Prescott defended Schottenheimer.

"It's all of us. Don't put the blame on one person," he told reporters . "I think that's weak. I think that's cowardly."

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones also defended Schottenheimer and called out the team for not doing their part.

"I will say that a lot of people let Brian down today," Jones said. "So, for whatever criticism we want to have of Brian, we can all get in line. And that was a total — to use a cliché — that was a total team effort out there for us. We have to be, for our fans, we have to be better than that when we've got our hands on a win and drop the ball."

Dallas led by 10 points halfway through the fourth quarter, but Arizona cut it to a six-point game with just over a minute to go. The Cardinals then marched down the field and scored a touchdown to tie it, leaving just six seconds on the clock.

Arizona missed what would have been the game-winning extra point, but it didn't matter as it managed to get the win in overtime.

The Cowboys dropped to 3-5 with the loss, and it is looking increasingly likely that Schottenheimer's second year at the helm is going to end in the regular season rather than the playoffs.

articles.title: Inspiring story of discipline: How Aaron Rodgers' obsessive attention to detail turned years of patient preparation into record-setting accuracy and one of the lowest interception rates in NFL history
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers threw 597 passes in 2018 and gave the ball away twice.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers threw 597 passes in 2018 and gave the ball away twice. That works out to a 0.3 percent interception rate, the lowest for a single season in league history. He also once went 402 straight attempts without an interception, another record. Now 42 and playing for the Steelers, he still sits at or near the top of the career list at roughly 1.4 percent. None of it was luck. It came from years of waiting, studying and refusing to force a throw.How Aaron Rodgers built the lowest interception rate the NFL has seenStart with the career numbers. Through Week 6 of 2026, Rodgers had 539 touchdown passes against 128 interceptions on 8,976 attempts. That is better than four touchdowns for every pick, and it is a record ratio. Few players last long enough to build a sample that big, and fewer still keep the error rate that low across it.The consistency matters more than any single year. He has led the NFL in lowest interception percentage six times, in 2009, 2014, 2018, 2019, 2020 and 2021. In 2011 he posted a 122.5 passer rating, a mark nobody has beaten, with 45 touchdowns and six interceptions. In his MVP seasons of 2020 and 2021 he threw five and four picks while piling up touchdowns.The title is not locked down, though. Jacoby Brissett has traded places with him at the top of the list. In December 2025, Pro Football Reference had Rodgers ahead by a sliver, 1.4208 percent to 1.4233. That is how thin the margin is, and it says a lot about how rare this level of care is.Three years on the bench taught him patienceThe habit started with a wait most first-round picks never have to endure. Green Bay took Rodgers 24th overall in 2005. Brett Favre was still the starter, so Rodgers spent three seasons watching, charting and keeping his mouth shut. He did not take over until 2008.That stretch looks like a delay on paper. It worked more like an apprenticeship. He saw how a gunslinger's best throws and worst throws came from the same instinct. He learned which risks were worth it and which only felt exciting in the moment.The seeds were there earlier too. At Cal he set school records for the lowest interception percentage, 1.43 percent in 2003 and 1.95 percent for his career. Protecting the football was never a trait he picked up late. It was the thing he built his game around from the start.The habits behind the numbers: smart risks and free playsRodgers rarely throws into a spot where a defender can win the play. When a window looks tight, he moves on, takes the checkdown or throws it away. Plenty of quarterbacks say that. Few do it on every snap for 15 years.His style of caution is different from the usual kind. PFF noted in 2016 that he was conservative in a different way than someone like Alex Smith, completing only four passes deep down the middle on 502 attempts. He still attacked, just along the sideline and underneath, where a miss is an incompletion instead of a turnover.Then there are the free plays. His hard count drew defenders offside year after year, and a free play lets a quarterback fire downfield with nothing to lose. A good share of his big gains came from that small piece of preparation, not from raw arm talent.Pre-snap work did the rest. He reads coverage before the ball is snapped, picks his target early and trusts the answer. Most of his interception avoidance happened before the play even began.Can he still protect the ball at 42?The honest answer is mostly yes, with some wobble. Last season in Pittsburgh he threw for 3,322 yards, 24 touchdowns and seven interceptions. That is a clean year, but it came with a shorter, quicker game. His average depth of target sat near 6.4 yards and his time to throw was among the fastest in the league. He has traded some of his old deep shots for safety, and that is a smart trade at his age.This year has been rougher. Through six games he had thrown five interceptions. That is a 2.9 percent rate, the highest of his career. A thin receiving group and a shaky offensive line explain part of it, since pressure turns careful throws into hurried ones. Even so, the career rate has barely moved. Among quarterbacks with 2,000 or more attempts, he still has the lowest rate ever, at 1.44 percent.The test now is whether a quarterback built on patience can keep his edge once the arm and the protection both slip a little. If anyone has the tools to manage it, he does. Twenty-one years in, he is still guarding the ball like a rookie fighting for a roster spot.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Updated 2027 NFL Draft Order After Week 8 Results, Who Could Chargers & Jets Take?
articles.summary: The New York Jets have become the big story in the 2027 NFL draft conversation after Week 8's results.
articles.body:
The New York Jets have become the big story in the 2027 NFL draft conversation after Week 8's results.

The Jets currently own the projected fourth, sixth and 10th picks in the April selection process thanks to losses by the Indianapolis Colts and Dallas Cowboys.

The Jets could be on the verge of landing an historic draft class if the Colts and Cowboys continue to lose. They own the first-round picks of both franchises through the trades for Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams.

The Los Angeles Chargers still sit atop the projected draft order with their 0-7 record. They are in front of the Tennessee Titans and Miami Dolphins as we near the halfway point of the NFL regular season.

4. New York Jets (via Indianapolis - 2-6)

Drew Mestemaker is emerging as potentially the best quarterback prospect in the draft class.

The Oklahoma State quarterback is second in the FBS in passing yards with 2,649 and tied for second in the FBS in touchdown passes with 25.

Mestemaker has put up better numbers than most of the other quarterbacks eligible for the 2027 NFL draft.

The North Texas transfer wasn't heavily recruited entering college, but over the last two years, he's become one of the most productive quarterbacks at the collegiate level.

Mestemaker has to be an intriguing option for the New York Jets, who would assumedly use one of their three first-round selections on a quarterback.

The Miami Dolphins, Tennessee Titans and other quarterback-needy teams should keep an eye on Mestemaker over the final few weeks of the college football season. He might turn out to be the best quarterback available given the struggles and injuries of the other players at his position.

Charlie Becker might end up as the best wide receiver prospect not named Jeremiah Smith.

The Indiana wide out is up to 875 yards and nine touchdowns on the season after his 149-yard, one-touchdown performance on Saturday.

Becker already eclipsed his career highs in receptions, receiving yards and touchdowns that he set a year ago with the Hoosiers.

The majority of teams at the top of the draft order will be interested in Smith, but Becker is a fascinating option for the franchises that miss out on the Ohio State player.

The Chargers could take Smith at No. 1, or if they land on Becker if they fall further down the draft order.

The Jets should have eyes on Becker as a complement to Garrett Wilson, especially if they focus on a quarterback with their first draft pick.

articles.body:
A 15-0 run led by Bo Nix capped a 28-24 Denver Broncos victory over Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday.

A missed field goal set up Nix and the Broncos' game-winning drive, as Nix and Jonah Coleman charged down the field to take the lead for the first time since Denver's opening 3-0 advantage.

The Broncos' game-sealing defensive stand, capped by a sack of Mahomes, secured the victory after Denver entered Sunday's home matchup as 1.5-point underdogs, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

The loss marked the Chiefs' second straight defeat after they fell 20-3 to the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks last week. The Chiefs dropped to 5-2 after winning five consecutive games to open the season.

The Broncos moved into first place in the AFC West with the win, improving to 6-2 and overtaking Kansas City who fell to second.

Both teams added a field goal and a touchdown in the second quarter, sending Kansas City into halftime with a 17-13 advantage.

Mahomes extended the Chiefs' lead in the second quarter with an explosive 73-yard touchdown pass to Emmett Johnson. Nix answered by finding Jaylen Waddle for a 1-yard touchdown on fourth-and-goal, keeping Denver within striking distance.

The Chiefs scored the third quarter's only touchdown, extending their lead to a two-score game on a touchdown pass to Noah Gray.

The Broncos struck first in the fourth quarter when Nix connected with Nate Adkins for a touchdown, followed by a successful two-point conversion to cut the deficit to a field goal.

The Chiefs burned 6:24 off the clock on their next drive, but a sack of Mahomes forced them into a difficult 54-yard field goal attempt. Harrison Butker missed, giving Nix and the Broncos prime field position with a chance to take the lead.

Nix immediately connected with Jonah Coleman for a 51-yard pass to move the Broncos into the Chiefs' red zone. Coleman capped the drive one play later with a 5-yard rushing touchdown, but Denver may have left too much time on the clock for Mahomes and the Chiefs.

Mahomes connected with Travis Kelce on a big pass to move the Chiefs down the field, but Kansas City could not convert from the Broncos' 1-yard line. Denver's defense stood tall at the goal line, finishing the game with a sack of Mahomes to seal the home win.

The Chiefs will host the New York Jets, while the Broncos will hit the road to face the Carolina Panthers next Sunday. Both games are scheduled to kick off at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Josh Jacobs' lawyers call police release of previously unreported abuse allegations 'character assassination'
articles.summary: Josh Jacobs' attorneys call the released police case file a "character assassination" and say the domestic abuse allegations are easily disproven.
articles.body: The attorneys representing Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs admitted that the recently released police case file that includes new allegations of domestic abuse from years ago are threatening the running back's career, but also see it as a case of "character assassination" that is easily disproven. That is the underlying point of a statement released Sunday afternoon by attorneys David Z. Chesnoff, Richard A. Schonfeld and Clarence F. Duchac III to the media, including OutKick and Fox News Digital. "The three accounts are old, are hearsay, and easily disproven, yet released to the media by police without any investigation to determine whether they were accurate or contradicted by evidence," the statement reads. "Josh is answering them in detail because of the character assassination that is occurring, unfairly threatening his career." NFL LIFTS ABUSE SUSPENSIONS ON GREEN BAY'S JOSH JACOBS AND DENVER'S JONATHON COOPER AS INVESTIGATIONS CONTINUE The NFL said in a statement Saturday that it is reviewing the previously unreported allegations that Jacobs physically abused multiple women whose existence came to light amid the investigation into the May 23 incident that was well-chronicled. The NFL was already investigating Jacobs for that May 23 incident in which Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor criminal damage to property connected to a domestic incident with an ex-girlfriend in Green Bay. Jacobs was convicted of the battery charge in September and spent six games on the commissioner’s exempt list this season. He has returned to the Packers, but the team has been among those keeping in contact with the Indianapolis Colts about trading for running back Jonathan Taylor. The Packers would not be interested in Taylor if they expected to keep Jacobs. PACKERS' INTEREST IN JONATHAN TAYLOR SHOWS DESIRE TO MOVE ON FROM JOSH JACOBS AND HIS DOMESTIC ABUSE ISSUES Understanding this, the statement takes aim at the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department's case file release to the media. "The file includes summaries of three telephone interviews describing events in 2021 and 2022," the statement from Jacobs' attorneys said. "Josh Jacobs denies all three accounts and has a substantial body of tangible evidence to back up his assertions. "The police department’s released file contains only phone interviews, taken years after the fact, with no additional investigation, save for an acknowledgment that Josh did nothing wrong. Josh was not given an opportunity to present evidence to Hobart-Lawrence in response to the uncorroborated report, primarily because Hobart-Lawrence took no action related to the unsupported and stale allegations." And then the details, according to the Jacobs side: "One of these three women made a claim to the NFL, which reviewed it and decided no action was warranted. Josh has kept evidence that supports his accounts and the NFL’s decision. Nothing in the released file indicates that any such evidence was used or even sought. Indeed, the police report did not even present any of this information. "Another woman made a claim in 2021, but only after Josh called the Las Vegas police to his home to report the woman for misconduct. A police report was written that day, which effectively undermined her claims. No further action was taken by any authority after she was removed from Josh’s home." The police file, per NBC26 in Wisconsin, claims a third woman told the police that Jacobs slapped her in the face, threw her onto a bed, threw her to the floor, spit on her and grabbed her throat in January 2022. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "Josh denies any physical altercation with the third woman," the statement from Jacobs' attorneys said. "She first contacted Josh and asked to visit. She came to Las Vegas and stayed at his home. Another person was present in the house during part of her stay. She stayed there overnight and left the following evening — on her own, in a car she ordered herself. The receipt for that ride is in the police file the department released, and it is consistent with Josh’s account of how the visit ended, not hers." It's clear the Jacobs camp understands the stakes: Their client's enduring status in the NFL. And they want to remind everyone that charges that resulted in a trial are the only history that should matter. "Josh took responsibility for what happened in May," the attorneys said. "He entered into an agreement with prosecutors for two misdemeanors, and he is meeting the court’s requirements." In his two games since returning to the 5–3 Packers, Jacobs has rushed 32 times for 75 yards and a touchdown, averaging just 2.3 yards per carry. The three-time Pro Bowler has been more productive as a receiver, catching 11 passes for 68 yards and two touchdowns. After scoring one of his touchdowns in the Packers' 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers on Thursday, Jacobs had a controversial touchdown celebration. He insisted he wasn't making light of his recent arrest and that the celebration was instead inspired by a gospel song. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Report Card Grades for Bills' Week 8 Game vs. Ravens
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills have won 12 consecutive games coming off the bye week.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills have won 12 consecutive games coming off the bye week.

That's the case after they blew out the Baltimore Ravens 36-10 on Sunday in a far-from-pristine performance against a team that was hardly competitive after losing two quarterbacks to injury in the first half.

Regardless, here are my grades for all of the key players from the victory.

It was an uneven and sometimes puzzling outing for Allen, who ultimately put up solid numbers with 289 passing yards, 30 rushing yards and three total touchdowns, but he also made several poor decisions and was off target more frequently than usual.

Allen's first-quarter interception was primarily the fault of tight end Jackson Hawes, but that pick wouldn't have occurred had Allen not fired a rocket behind his intended target.

Later, he overthrew Keon Coleman on what would have been a home-run touchdown, nearly threw an interception at the goal line, and failed to see several wide-open targets on incompletions (one of which would have resulted in a huge gain for James Cook, but instead led to a downfield injury for Josh Palmer).

Allen looked hesitant on several option plays and scrambles, ultimately costing the offense in a few of those spots.

He did make up for a lot of that with several hero plays down the stretch, including some dimes to Dalton Kincaid and DJ Moore to ice the game in the fourth quarter. But all in all, it wasn't a performance he'd submit to Hall of Fame voters.

Cook did not have a lot of room to work with for much of the day, but the veteran still managed 102 scrimmage yards on 23 touches. It looks as though he avoided what could have been a scary injury in the fourth quarter, and he managed to bounce back from a mid-game lull with 28 yards on his final six rushes (plus a nine-yard gain that was wiped out by a penalty).

It was also another turnover-free performance, which is encouraging considering his ball-security issues dating back a calendar year.

Not only did the backup average a team-best 5.0 yards per attempt on six carries, but he lost credit for a sweet 12-yard slash that was negated by a holding penalty in the fourth quarter. Davis really helped the Bills put this game away, and I'd like to see more of him going forward.

He did take a swing pass for 18 yards on a fourth-down play late in the first half, but Johnson generated just five yards on six touches outside of that.

The veteran did catch four passes for 82 yards and a touchdown in his return from injury, and he made an unbelievable grab on a contested play downfield on a third-quarter scoring drive. Still, Moore left some plays on the field (he was targeted seven times) and had an avoidable fumble late in the first half. It's also possible he's hurt again, which doesn't impact his grade but has to be a concern based on how often he's been injured already this season.

A victim of Moore's return, he was targeted only three times and finished with a single four-yard reception. But he did get open on what might have been a 74-yard touchdown if Allen hadn't overthrown him.

Shakir was in a zone on Sunday. He made a few critical receptions in traffic and picked up crucial yardage with second efforts and sharp cuts after the catch. He ultimately caught five passes on six targets for 64 yards, but his impact went well beyond that.

That aforementioned 18-yard swing play for Ty Johnson? Shakir played a huge role as a blocker.

It was actually Kincaid who threw the other key block on that Johnson catch-and-run, but that moment was easily overshadowed by a four-catch, 86-yard effort that included the game-icing touchdown in the fourth quarter. However, he loses the A due to a really brutal drop in the red zone, as well as another semi-drop in the first quarter.

Knox also had a drop, catching just one pass for six yards. He did, however, continue to do fine work in pass protection and as a tush-push maestro.

He's taking a lot of heat for tipping an interception into the air, but the pass was inaccurate and behind him. His blocking remained solid, which is his primary role on this offense. Still, that freak turnover and a holding penalty count against him.

Dawkins did tremendous work maximizing Allen's hang-in time on that critical play that resulted in a highlight-reel Moore catch on a third-quarter scoring drive. He was solid throughout the day in pass protection but did have some trouble as a run blocker and took what could have been a very costly false-start penalty in the red zone early.

He was often overmatched in the running game but again proved to be feisty and tough in a strong performance in pass protection. I didn't count a single pressure on Anderson.

On several key plays in crunch time, McGovern was the pivotal blocker on crucial runs for Cook and Davis. He was also a monster on Moore's fourth-quarter touchdown play.

He and the entire interior struggled to open up lanes for much of the first half, and a fourth-quarter holding penalty didn't help Torrence's cause. He's saved by a strong showing as a pass blocker.

Making his first start of the season in place of the injured Spencer Brown, Grable was not the problem. The 2024 sixth-round pick could have done more to help an overpowered Hawes on a third-quarter holding penalty, but he looked like a suitable starter overall.

He got his hand on the quarterback once and brought the pressure on a Deone Walker strip-sack that was ultimately overturned on replay. And he's certainly more of an asset than a liability against the run. But it was still another quiet game overall for a veteran who hasn't recorded a sack since Week 2.

The heart and soul of this defense took Lamar Jackson out on Baltimore's first play from scrimmage. He was an absolute force when the Bills were putting the game away in the second half, and it's important to acknowledge he made a couple of key plays on Derrick Henry in run defense, too.

A successful blitz from Dorian Williams was the primary force behind Parker's second-quarter sack on Joe Fagnano, but the 22-year-old rookie completed the play and deserves credit for that. He didn't make a positive impact beyond that despite being on the field for 25 snaps, and he was flagged for being offside late in the first half.

His second-half strip-sack on Fagnano was overturned but it was still another high-impact game for the emerging star. I noted two particular third-down plays in which Walker was a disruptive force, causing the Ravens to punt it away. The motor is always running for the big guy. An encroachment penalty in the red zone was the only real blemish on Sunday.

There were a couple of vintage Oliver moments in his return from a knee injury, but he played just 20 snaps as he's being eased back in. He wasn't a factor beyond the occasional effective rush.

I have four full pages of notes from this game. Sanders' name isn't mentioned once despite the fact he played 21 snaps. He was a ghost, but there were also no killer mistakes.

I actually loved the work Jackson did against Henry, especially early in the game. And he added a second-quarter sack that likely took Baltimore points off the board.

It felt as though Bernard brought more energy to this game than all of the previous six combined. He was a heat-seeking missile, consistently making plays as a pass rusher and run defender. His tackling comes and goes, but I'm not heavily faulting him for a very questionable low-block penalty in the second half.

It appears as though something clicked for Bernard during the bye week. His aggressiveness was costly on a couple of occasions Sunday, and he was overmatched here and there, but the good certainly outweighed the bad.

Parker's sack was tied directly to a great blitz from Williams, but the 25-year-old continues to be bullied in run defense. He was just not able to hang on several strong plays from Henry in this game. It's a roller-coaster ride with this guy, but this was not an overly problematic performance altogether.

It's not easy to grade cornerbacks against a third-string quarterback making his debut as an undrafted rookie, but it was practically a perfect day for Benford in terms of coverage.

Close to the same story for the rookie, who recorded his first career interception on a play that was generated by Geno Stone. Igbinosun whiffed on a tackle that resulted in a Justice Hill first down and probably got away with a pass interference penalty late in the first half, but it was a net-positive showing.

What an introduction! In Couch's debut as a position player, he stepped in for Dee Alford in the slot and was the primary reason why Zay Flowers had the first zero-catch game of his career (and on five targets, no less). He was also a sure tackler. There's a good chance that when Alford returns, Couch remains in the mix at Maxwell Hairston's expense.

Bishop has steadily picked up his game following a slow start, and this was easily his best outing of the season to date. That second-quarter strip sack on Tyler Huntley was a thing of beauty, and I didn't spot a mistake beyond that.

He takes a lot of heat, but Hamlin did his job with C.J. Gardner-Johnson out of the lineup. And while the competition wasn't overwhelming, he had a big responsibility with lots of work involving Flowers. Zero complaints here.

As with Couch, we'll want to see Stone against an offense that isn't using a third-string quarterback before drawing grand conclusions. Still, Stone was awesome in his debut with the team after being elevated from the practice squad.

He showed great instincts on a near-pick that resulted in Igbinosun's interception and had a tremendous open-field tackle for loss on Hill to force a Baltimore punt and set the tone early.

The guy co-led the team with six tackles despite playing just 19 snaps.

The veteran successfully doinked in a 56-yarder and nailed every other kick he was tasked with on another perfect afternoon.

Two fine punts from the rookie, both resulting in the Ravens starting at the 23-yard line. No problem there, even if it wasn't a herculean effort.

He had three strong punt returns, gaining eight, 15 and 17 yards on his three attempts in an error-free showing.

articles.title: “We positioned Travis to be world famous”: How Travis Kelce built a business empire beyond the NFL with help from two brothers who saw his potential early
articles.summary: Travis Kelce is no longer just the Kansas City Chiefs tight end known for making big plays.
articles.body: Travis Kelce is no longer just the Kansas City Chiefs tight end known for making big plays. He has moved into fashion, business and entertainment, with ventures such as Tru Kolors and Garage Beer adding to his growing profile. But this off-field career did not come together overnight. Andre and Aaron Eanes saw an opportunity in Kelce years before his NFL fame and built a plan to turn his personality into a brand that could reach far beyond football.Their story with Kelce began at the University of Cincinnati. What started as a college friendship eventually became a business partnership that helped shape the tight end's career outside the NFL. How Andre and Aaron Eanes saw a bigger opportunity in Travis KelceAndre first met Travis Kelce through D.J. Woods, the tight end's college roommate and Andre's childhood friend. The two became close at Cincinnati, where Andre was building an event management business. He helped Kelce and his teammates get into parties and other events.Their connection went beyond the social scene. Andscape reported on November 20, 2023, that Andre and Travis Kelce also worked together at a call centre during the period when Cincinnati suspended the tight end from football in 2010 after a failed drug test.Andre and his twin brother Aaron had launched A&A Management in 2011. They wanted to help athletes build businesses and careers that could last beyond their playing days. Kelce became their second client as he prepared for the 2013 NFL Draft.Aaron had a different idea of what athlete management could look like. In a New York Times profile published on January 2, 2024, he explained, "Agents are contract advisers. I thought instead about a music model and building a business where there's coordination with all their external providers."The brothers wanted to handle more than contract negotiations. They focused on commercials, public appearances, media opportunities and other ways to grow Kelce's name. Their ambition was to make him as recognisable as Dwayne Johnson.Andre explained the thinking in the same New York Times profile: "We positioned Travis to be world famous. We didn't know how it would happen, or when it would happen, or what would help push that further along. But it's always been the thought in the back of our minds."How Travis Kelce took that vision into fashion, beer and other businessThe brothers' strategy gave Kelce a platform beyond the football field. His commercial work and television appearances helped introduce him to people who did not necessarily follow the Chiefs. He hosted Saturday Night Live in March 2023 and continued to expand his media presence through the New Heights podcast with Jason Kelce.Aaron also explained why he wanted brands to see Kelce as more than an athlete. In Andscape's November 20, 2023, report, he said, "We had a strategy of we want to maximize national commercials to parlay his characters and his ability to be talent throughout the season so that when people are seeing him, they're seeing him as talent, not as the football player."That thinking fits the business interests Kelce has developed. He founded Tru Kolors, his sportswear and lifestyle brand, in 2019. On August 27, 2025, the label teamed up with American Eagle for a limited-edition collection. Kelce served as creative director and took part in the design process.He also entered the beer business with Jason. On June 12, 2024, the brothers announced they had become significant investors, owners and operators of Garage Beer, an Ohio-based brand. The deal gave them roles in areas such as marketing, sales, distribution and expansion.Aaron had a simple response when people described the previous year as unusually hectic. In the January 2, 2024, New York Times profile, he said, "Actually, it's not that crazy." He added, "It's because it's easy when you have a plan. We're executing that plan."The Eanes brothers did not build Tru Kolors or Garage Beer for him. Instead, they helped create a management strategy that gave him room to pursue opportunities beyond football. And the plan they began with a college connection has grown into a business relationship that continues to shape his life outside the NFL.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. While the star player has been busy with his career, his investment in Six Flags has also hit a new low as the company tries to protect itself.Travis Kelce backed Six Flags makes a move to protect itself amid tragic deaths at the parkJust last month, a 42 year old schoolteacher from Atlanta Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem was killed at Six Flags Over Georgia after being ejected from the infamous rollercoaster, Goliath.Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem hit four other passengers as he was ejected from his seat and minutes later, fell to his tragic death.While Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem’s unfortunate death has again raised concerns about the safety measures that Six Flags has been taking, the company has announced that it will finally be adding seatbelts on their infamous rollercoaster.Six Flags CEO John Reilly posted the update in a letter as he wrote, “We have engaged independent engineers and ride inspection specialists to comprehensively review current safety procedures across our entire portfolio of rides and attractions, across all of our parks…”Six Flags CEO John Reilly added, “We are committed to carefully evaluating their findings and taking appropriate action to further strengthen our standards and culture of safety.”Six Flags CEO John Reilly continued in the letter, “What happened has deeply affected all of us at Six Flags…Safety has always been fundamental to the experience we provide for our guests. articles.title: Jerry Jones and Dallas Cowboys face tight end crisis after ankle injury forces key starter out in shocking loss to Arizona Cardinals
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys suffered another frustrating setback after losing 33-30 to the Arizona Cardinals in overtime on Sunday, November 1.
articles.body: The Dallas Cowboys suffered another frustrating setback after losing 33-30 to the Arizona Cardinals in overtime on Sunday, November 1. The defeat dropped Dallas to 3-5, but the result was not the only concern coming out of Week 8. The team also lost a key option at tight end after an ankle injury forced him out of the game.Jake Ferguson left during Dallas’ opening offensive possession and eventually was ruled out for the remainder of the contest. With backup Luke Schoonmaker already inactive because of a groin injury, the Cowboys had limited options at the position for the rest of the afternoon. The situation could create another problem as Dallas prepares for its Week 9 trip to Indianapolis. Dallas Cowboys lose Jake Ferguson after opening-drive injuryFerguson picked up the ankle injury on the Cowboys’ first offensive drive against Arizona. He initially went to the sideline before heading to the locker room with members of the training staff. He later returned to the field, but his afternoon ended early.According to R.J. Coyle of The Dallas Morning News, Ferguson was ruled out for the remainder of the game. He did not record a catch or receive a target before leaving.The 27-year-old had recorded 17 receptions for 115 yards and three touchdowns through seven games this season. Those numbers have been below his usual production, but Ferguson remains an important part of the Cowboys’ passing attack. His ability to work underneath and provide Prescott with another option over the middle gives the offense flexibility.His absence became more difficult to manage because Schoonmaker was unavailable. That left Brevyn Spann-Ford and James Mitchell as the two healthy tight ends available to Dallas against Arizona.Spann-Ford took on a larger role and finished with four receptions for 31 yards. Mitchell also made a contribution, recovering Javonte Williams’ fumble in the end zone for a touchdown.The Cowboys managed to get contributions from their remaining options, but losing two tight ends in the same game leaves the position short on depth. Ferguson’s injury status will now be watched ahead of the next matchup. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported that Ferguson suffered a low-ankle sprain, although his availability for the Colts game has not been confirmed. Dallas Cowboys face more pressure after painful Cardinals defeatThe injury added to an afternoon that quickly turned into a difficult one for Dallas. The Cowboys appeared to have control after building a 17-3 lead, but Arizona fought back and forced overtime.The Cardinals tied the game at 30-30 with six seconds remaining in regulation after Gardner Minshew connected with Michael Wilson for a touchdown. Chad Ryland missed the extra point that could have won the game, giving Dallas another chance to escape with a victory.However, neither team scored on its first overtime possession. Arizona eventually moved into field-goal range, and Ryland made a 42-yard kick to seal the 33-30 win.Dak Prescott finished with 195 passing yards and a touchdown on 19 completions from 29 attempts. CeeDee Lamb caught seven passes for 58 yards, while George Pickens added two receptions for 48 yards.The defeat left Dallas with a 3-5 record and another difficult week ahead. The team will travel to face the Indianapolis Colts on November 8, with the tight end situation among the issues to monitor.Ferguson's absence would put more responsibility on Spann-Ford and Mitchell if he cannot return. Dallas will also need to keep an eye on Schoonmaker's recovery from his groin injury.The Cowboys have not confirmed that Ferguson will miss the next game. For now, the immediate concern is his ankle injury and how quickly he can recover. With the team already struggling to turn promising performances into wins, another absence could make the road ahead even tougher.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes has earned more than almost any player in NFL history, and a lot of it is going into things that will outlast his playing days.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has earned more than almost any player in NFL history, and a lot of it is going into things that will outlast his playing days. Some sits in Kansas City sports teams. Some runs through the foundation he leads with his wife, Brittany. His 2023 contract restructure came with a $1.625 million gift to Boys & Girls Clubs of America, which showed how the pieces fit. With three young children at home, the long game looks like a family project. He has not framed it that way in public, yet the pattern is hard to miss.Patrick Mahomes is building wealth that lasts beyond footballThe headline number came in 2020, when Mahomes signed a 10-year extension that could reach $503 million. What he does with the money tells you more. Even great quarterbacks get a short window, and Mahomes has treated his paychecks like seed money.In 2023 he agreed to a restructured deal that eased the Chiefs' cap pressure. Winning keeps his value high, and his value feeds everything else.He holds minority stakes in the Kansas City Royals and Sporting KC. Brittany is a co-owner of the Kansas City Current in the National Women's Soccer League. Stakes like these tend to gain value as leagues grow, and they pay off whether or not he throws a pass.That is the slow part of the plan. Plenty of retired players learn that income stops when the contract does. Mahomes has built money that keeps coming without him on the field.Where the foundation fits inThe 15 and the Mahomies Foundation focuses on children's health, wellness and underserved communities. The $1.625 million gift to Boys & Girls Clubs came with a multi-year commitment, so it is not a one-time photo op. Mahomes said the partnership was about "investing in the future of children."He first talked about the foundation on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, describing it as something built around kids. The work led to his nomination for the Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year award in 2022.Closer to home, the foundation helped fund new voting machines so Arrowhead Stadium can serve as a polling site for at least the next 10 to 12 years. It is an odd thing for a quarterback to fund. It is also the kind of project that keeps working long after the cameras leave, and rarely trends on social media.What it could mean for his three kidsSterling Skye, Bronze and Golden Raye are all young. Sterling was born in February 2021, so she turned five this year. Nobody knows what any of them will want to do.Mahomes grew up in Texas, yet he keeps tying his money to Kansas City. Brittany does too. That roots the kids in one place, which is not common for athlete families, who often move.That is where the structure makes sense. Ownership stakes can grow while the kids do. A foundation gives the family work in Kansas City that has nothing to do with a scoreboard, and gives the kids a chance to see giving back up close. Together they keep options open.To be fair, Mahomes has never laid out a family wealth plan in public. That link is my read of the pattern, not something he has said. The deal he signed in 2020 runs into 2031, when Sterling turns ten. By then, we will know whether this was a plan or just good habits.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “He's struggled a little bit”: Kansas City Chiefs face Harrison Butker dilemma after costly Denver Broncos miss as Justin Tucker waits for his opportunity
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs have a difficult decision to make after Harrison Butker missed a crucial 54-yard field goal against the Denver Broncos.
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs have a difficult decision to make after Harrison Butker missed a crucial 54-yard field goal against the Denver Broncos. The miss came with 2:31 remaining and gave Denver another chance to take control. The Broncos scored a touchdown two plays later and won 28-24, leaving Kansas City with another painful loss.Butker's position now faces fresh scrutiny, especially after the Chiefs signed former Baltimore Ravens kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad on October 28. Andy Reid has backed Butker publicly, but his earlier comments suggest the coaching staff is no longer treating the starting job as untouchable. Andy Reid's warning puts Harrison Butker's starting job under pressureReid had already raised concerns about Butker's performances before the Denver game. Speaking to reporters on October 28, following the Chiefs' decision to bring in Tucker, the head coach admitted that his regular kicker needed to improve."Right now, his technique's off a bit. It's not as consistent as he wants it. Things happen," Reid said, according to KMBC.The Chiefs coach also explained why the team brought Tucker into the building despite his support for Butker."He's one of my favorite guys," Reid said. "And sometimes things don't go quite the way you want them, and you work on that. So, he understands the business and how it works. And we had a practice squad position open, and so, for security we brought (Tucker) in and put him in that spot that we had open. Butker gets it."Reid then made his expectations clear: "He gets it, and he knows that's part of this business. He's struggled a little bit. He gets it. He needs to pick it up here a little bit."The comments came after Butker missed two field goals against Seattle on October 25. He then missed another against Denver, making his position even harder to defend. Justin Tucker's arrival adds pressure as Chiefs weigh Harrison Butker's contractTucker offers Kansas City an experienced alternative. The seven-time Pro Bowler has converted 89.1% of his career field-goal attempts, although his final season with Baltimore in 2024 was difficult. He made only 22 of 30 attempts.His signing also drew criticism following allegations from 16 massage therapists. Tucker denied the allegations and served a 10-game suspension in 2025 for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy.Speaking to reporters on October 28, Reid addressed the controversy, saying, "He's done his suspension. ... I'll leave it at that for you." He added that the Chiefs had spoken to people and completed their checks before signing Tucker.Money also complicates Butker's situation. Over The Cap lists his 2026 base salary at $5.805 million, which is fully guaranteed. His four-year extension runs through 2028 and carries a total value of $25.6 million.The Chiefs have not announced a change at kicker. However, with Tucker waiting and Butker struggling, the November 8 game against the New York Jets could become another important test for the veteran.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Lawyers Say Packers' Josh Jacobs Has 'Tangible Evidence' Disputing Allegations From Other Women
articles.summary: Lawyers for Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs say he has a "substantial body of tangible evidence" disputing the allegations three women made against him while police were investigating his battery case.
articles.body:
Lawyers for Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs say he has a "substantial body of tangible evidence" disputing the allegations three women made against him while police were investigating his battery case.

Jacobs pleaded no contest on Sept. 10 to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend, who said he threw her to the ground. In response to a public records request, the Hobart-Lawrence (Wisconsin) Police Department released records from their investigation Friday night that included the accounts of three other women who reported similar allegations from years before.

After spending the first six games of the season on the commissioner's exempt list, which prevented him from playing or practicing, Jacobs has returned to play in the Packers' last two games. The NFL has said its investigation into Jacobs is ongoing, which means he still could be subject to more discipline from the league.

Jacobs' lawyers — David Z. Chesnoff, Richard A. Schonfeld and Clarence F. Duchac III — issued a statement Saturday noting that the Brown County District Attorney's office had "these uncorroborated, old, and previously unreported allegations for months." They issued another statement Sunday that went into more detail.

"Josh took responsibility for what happened in May," the lawyers said. "He entered into an agreement with prosecutors for two misdemeanors, and he is meeting the court's requirements.

"The three accounts are old, are hearsay, and easily disproven, yet released to the media by police without any investigation to determine whether they were accurate or contradicted by evidence. Josh is answering them in detail because of the character assassination that is occurring, unfairly threatening his career."

Jacobs' lawyers said that one of the three women made a claim to the NFL, which reviewed it and decided no action was warranted. They said Jacobs "has kept evidence that supports his accounts and the NFL's decision."

The NFL declined comment Sunday on the lawyers' statement. After Hobart-Lawrence police released the records that detailed the accounts from other women, NFL spokesman Brian McCarthy had said Saturday that the league would review these allegations as part of its investigation.

Jacobs' lawyers said another woman made a claim only after Jacobs had called Las Vegas police to his home to report her for misconduct. Jacobs played for the Las Vegas Raiders before joining the Packers in 2024.

Jacobs also denied any physical altercation with the third woman. Jacobs' lawyers said she contacted Jacobs to ask to visit, came to Las Vegas and stayed at his home, and that another person was present in the house for part of her stay.

According to the records released Friday, one woman contacted police after Jacobs' arrest to say she had experienced a similar incident with him around 2023. She later would say the incident actually occurred on Jan. 5, 2022.

The woman said she had communicated with Jacobs for about six months before spending around 11 hours at his home. The woman said that after she told Jacobs she hadn't come there for sex, he became angry, slapped her and told her not to disrespect him.

She said he took her phone and threw it into a swimming pool when she attempted to leave, and that he grabbed her by the hair, threw her onto a bed, pinned her down, threw her to the floor and said, "I should kill you right now." She said Jacobs also spit on her.

The woman said she hadn't previously reported the incident to law enforcement because she remained friends with Jacobs afterward and was concerned her allegations wouldn't be believed. The woman said she contacted police this time because she believed it showed a pattern of behavior similar to the allegations in the May case.

Another woman told police she had sex with Jacobs in April 2021. The woman said his condom broke, so she told Jacobs to get tested for sexually transmitted diseases because they both had been involved with other people.

The woman said Jacobs later removed her from the residence, grabbed her by the arms and bicep area, pushed her against a wall and threw her belongings out. She told police that she sustained bruises to her arms and swelling in her rib area.

Hobart/Lawrence police said they obtained records from that incident indicating that officers observed "no visible signs of injury, bruising or damage consistent with a physical altercation."

Another woman said she met Jacobs through social media and that he flew her to a residence in May 2022. She described an altercation in which Jacobs grabbed her by the hair, placed his hands on her head and neck, dragged her, scratched her chest and took her phone after it fell to the floor.

She said she didn't report the incident to police because she wasn't a U.S. citizen at the time and Jacobs told her she could be deported.

Jacobs was arrested May 26, three days after Hobart-Lawrence police officers came to his Wisconsin home to investigate a disturbance. According to police, the woman told them Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground as she was trying to exit a garage door, causing her to hit her head. Police said Jacobs also took her phone from her while she was on the ground.

Police said they noticed redness on her face and neck and could feel a bump on the back of her head.

According to a criminal complaint, the woman's statement was corroborated by surveillance footage from the camera system in the garage where the incident occurred. Both Jacobs and the victim have gone to court in an attempt to permanently seal evidence from the case, including video footage.

articles.title: It looked like more Mahomes magic. Then the Broncos won a nail-biter — again.
articles.summary: In a season full of one-score games, the Denver Broncos outlasted Kansas City on the final play. Denver has the league’s best record in close games.
articles.body: A familiar script was playing out again Sunday afternoon in Denver. Trailing 28-24 with 4 seconds to play and the ball at the 1-yard line, Kansas City put the ball in the hands of quarterback Patrick Mahomes expecting the type of late comeback victory on which he has built a career. Mahomes threw for a go-ahead touchdown — until a flag for a false start was thrown just as his receiver, Rashee Rice, caught the would-be game-winning pass. Backed up 5 yards and given a final play to decide the AFC West showdown, Mahomes dropped back to pass but this time was sacked to send the Chiefs to 5-2 and the Broncos to 6-2. The ending was particularly nail-biting. But it was just one close game in a season full of them. It was the 71st game of this season decided by one score or less — tying the record for the most through Week 8 since the 1970 merger. The spotlight will all be on the final three plays. Before the game-ending sack, Denver stuffed star Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III on a short attempt from the 1-yard line, leading to the play on which a flinch by offensive tackle Jaylon Moore earned a false-start flag and negated Kansas City’s go-ahead touchdown. “I didn’t see it,” Chiefs coach Andy Reid said. “I saw him move his head, but I didn’t see” a penalty. The narrow outcome also will spark more debate about the job security of Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker. When Butker, Kansas City’s kicker since 2017, signed a four-year contract reported to be worth more than $25 million in 2024, he’d made 89.1% of his field goal attempts while helping the Chiefs win three Super Bowls. In three years since then, his accuracy had fallen to 82%, including just 9 of 19 on attempts of 50-plus yards. This season, he’d made 11 of his 16 tries overall, and he was 2 for 6 from 50-plus yards. His accuracy was concerning enough that Kansas City last week signed veteran kicker Justin Tucker to its practice squad as a not-so-subtle way to increase the competition on Butker, even though Tucker hadn’t played in more than a year following suspension for his off-field conduct. Butker had made a 45-yard attempt earlier in the game, but with Kansas City leading 24-21 with 2:36 left in regulation, he missed a 54-yard attempt that would have padded the lead. Denver then drove 56 yards in just two plays to go ahead 28-24, leaving Kansas City 116 seconds for a comeback. When Denver’s goal-line stand held firm after it sacked Mahomes on the final play, the game became the 35th of this season with a game-winning score in the final four minutes of the fourth quarter or in overtime. (The NFL record through eight weeks is 36.) Perhaps the ending, as wild as it was, should have been expected. Over the past two seasons, Denver’s 16-2 record in one-score games is the league’s best. “It has to come from we’ve done it before,” Broncos coach Sean Payton said.

articles.title: Justin Jefferson's Frustration Addressed By Kyler Murray After Vikings' Loss vs. Lions
articles.summary: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray said he understood Justin Jefferson's frustrations regarding Sunday's 19-15 loss against the Detroit Lions and some of the issues with the offense in general this season.
articles.body:
Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray said he understood Justin Jefferson's frustrations regarding Sunday's 19-15 loss against the Detroit Lions and some of the issues with the offense in general this season.

"We gotta find ways to get him the ball," Murray told reporters . "Obviously they're gonna double him, and they did today. Doubled a couple of guys today. And that's just part of it. This is my first year with him. Obviously [head coach Kevin O'Connell] and everybody that's been here understands how he gets treated and how he gets played [by opposing defenses]. But yeah, we gotta find ways to get him the ball. Obviously he's frustrated, and that's understandable. He is who he is, and he has every right to feel the way he feels when he doesn't get the ball."

Jefferson, 27, was targeted nine times during Sunday's loss, pulling down five receptions for 33 yards and a touchdown. But he has yet to record a 100-yard game this season and has just 28 catches for 335 yards and four touchdowns in six appearances.

According to ESPN's Kevin Seifert , Jefferson has "already has doubled his touchdown output this season (four) when compared with 2025 but otherwise is off to the worst start in his career. His average of 60.6 yards in the five full games he has played in 2026 is 20 yards per game lower than his next-worst season through Week 8."

The Vikings came into the matchup with the Lions a perfect 6-0, buoyed by excellent defensive play and strong special teams. That provided some cover for an offense that has not been good this season.

"We had some opportunities for [Jefferson], and there were some chances there," O'Connell told reporters after the loss. "But we've got to find a way to get him the ball, especially on potential chances for him on some of those sequences where we're looking to kick off some momentum. He's a great guy to do it behind, and we'll continue to find ways to get him the football. But it was a division game. These guys want to win. I don't fault the frustration or the competitiveness in any way, shape or form."

Jefferson, meanwhile, didn't speak to reporters after the game, a strong indication that he was more than a little frustrated. And it's understandable—the Vikings have a Lambo in the driveway and are taking it to get groceries occasionally but avoiding the highway.

How much of that falls on the play of Murray and how much of it is about the offensive scheme is up for debate. Whatever the main culprit, Jefferson's patience is clearly wearing thin.

articles.title: Harrison Butker Addresses Crucial Missed FG Amid Struggles After Chiefs' Loss vs. Broncos
articles.summary: Harrison Butker's job as the Kansas City Chiefs' kicker has already been at risk in recent weeks, and he didn't do himself any favors on Sunday.
articles.body:
Harrison Butker's job as the Kansas City Chiefs' kicker has already been at risk in recent weeks, and he didn't do himself any favors on Sunday.

Butker missed a crucial field goal late in the game against the Denver Broncos, and the Chiefs went on to lose 28-24. He took ownership of the miss after the game, saying it was "not good enough." Butker added that the weather wasn't a factor in the miss.

The miss came just days after the Chiefs signed veteran kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad amid Butker's struggles. That surely was a blow to his confidence, but he said he has to keep his focus on just making kicks.

"I try not to think about that. I try to focus on every kick, one kick at a time," he said. "Had the extra points and that field goal, but just a really bad miss on the 54, whatever it was."

Butker, who has been the Chiefs' kicker since 2017, has already missed six field goals this year and one extra point. He only missed five field goals total last year.

Whether the miss on Sunday will be enough for the Chiefs to move to a different kicker remains to be seen.

articles.title: Commanders Beat Eagles, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Jayden Daniels, Saquon, Top Players
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles dropped their sixth straight game of the season on Sunday night, falling 27-10 to Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles dropped their sixth straight game of the season on Sunday night, falling 27-10 to Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium.

The Commanders entered Sunday night's NFC East matchup as 5.5-point favorites over the injury-depleted Eagles, according to FanDuel Sportsbook.

The Eagles remained without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts, who was diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli. The condition involved blood clots in his left calf that traveled to his lungs, according to a joint statement from Hurts' agent Nicole Lynn and the Eagles.

Tanner McKee, a sixth-round pick out of Stanford in 2023, stepped in for Hurts and made his third consecutive start in his absence. However, McKee struggled to get the Eagles' offense going, as he was held to just 177 yards through the air and the team committed two turnovers.

The Eagles fell to 2-6 on the season, while the Commanders earned their second win, improving to 2-4-1.

1. NYG: 4-2-1 (OVR), 1-0-1 (DIV), 2-2-1 (CONF)

2. DAL: 3-5 (OVR), 2-1 (DIV), 2-4 (CONF)

3. WSH: 2-4-1 (OVR), 1-2-1 (DIV), 2-3-1 (CONF)

4. PHI: 2-6 (OVR), 1-2 (DIV), 1-5 (CONF)

The first quarter was chaotic for Washington, which missed a 55-yard field goal on its opening drive before tight end Chig Okonkwo fumbled the ball away. The turnover set up a quick 1:02 Eagles drive, capped by a Saquon Barkley touchdown.

Philadelphia took a 10-3 lead into the second quarter, both teams notching field goals.

The Commanders responded in the second quarter, rallying to take a 13-10 lead into halftime. Stefon Diggs hauled in a touchdown pass from Daniels to tie the game, and Washington added a field goal before the break.

The Eagles' offensive struggles continued after halftime, as they remained scoreless since the 4:27 mark of the first quarter. McKee was also sacked and fumbled the ball away, allowing Washington to capitalize with a field goal and extend its lead to six points heading into the final quarter.

After a 7:35 drive, Philadelphia's Jake Elliott missed a 41-yard field goal attempt. The Commanders responded with a lengthy drive of their own, capped by a 42-yard field goal from Drew Stevens.

The Commanders capped the win with a late interception on McKee, turning it into a touchdown by Rachaad White just 26 seconds later, followed by a successful two-point conversion from Austin Ekeler.

Washington will host the Los Angeles Rams next Sunday, while Philadelphia will welcome the New York Giants. Both games are scheduled to kick off at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: 5 Takeaways From Buccaneers’ Throwback Win Over Atlanta Falcons
articles.summary: The Bucs earned a huge win over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. Here are my five biggest takeaways from the game.
articles.body:
On Sunday, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers proved you can win a game in the NFL without having much of a passing attack.

Or, in the Bucs' case, without having any passing attack at all.

Tampa turned back the clock against the Atlanta Falcons and accomplished something that hasn't happened in the NFL in over 50 years .

The Bucs became the first team to win an NFL game without completing a pass since the Buffalo Bills did it against the New York Jets in 1974.

Who was the Jets' quarterback in that game?

It was a throwback win like we haven't seen in a long time. It was also a crucial win for the Bucs, who are now only a half-game out of first place in the NFC South.

Here are my five biggest takeaways from the Buccaneers' win over the Falcons:

1. The Bucs have a special running back duo: When Tampa signed Kenny Gainwell as a free agent this offseason, it was thought that he and Bucky Irving would be one of the most electric RB duos in the NFL.

However, Gainwell barely got any touches in the first six weeks. In Tampa's first six games, Gainwell was given only 19 total carries, which he turned into 61 rushing yards.

Over the last two games, both Tampa wins, Gainwell has a total of 39 carries for 228 yards, including a career-high 140 against Atlanta.

Irving has been a star all season and led the Bucs with 170 rushing yards on 27 carries against Atlanta. He also scored the Bucs' lone touchdown. Irving now has 51 rushes for 276 yards and three TDs over the last two games.

That is over 500 combined rushing yards for Irving and Gainwell in only two weeks.

If that's not a special RB tandem, I don't know what is.

2. The defense is outstanding: Tampa's defense has been a strength of the team all season. However, it was easy to overlook just how well the defense was playing because the team was 1-5.

The Bucs' defense has proven it can step up in different ways. The run defense is second-best in the NFL. In Weeks 6 and 7, Tampa notched five sacks in each game after only getting a total of six in the first five games.

While the Bucs recorded zero sacks against the Falcons, the defense intercepted Michael Penix Jr. four times on Sunday.

Linebacker Alex Anzalone had two of them. Starting cornerbacks Zyon McCollum and Jacob Parrish, who have been great all season, each recorded one.

3. Bucs are NFC South favorites once again : The Bucs were overwhelming favorites to win their division before the season began but got off to an abysmal 1-5 start.

However, the division is again the weakest in the NFL, which kept the door open for Tampa to get back into the race. After consecutive wins over the Panthers and Falcons, the Bucs are only a half-game out of first place and should be considered the favorites to win the division.

4. Todd Bowles deserves credit : Bowles looked like a dead man walking over the first few weeks of the season. It seemed like only a matter of time before he would be replaced.

However, he deserves a lot of credit for getting his defense to once again be one of the NFL's best and for keeping the team focused and together despite all the team's issues.

5. Need more from Baker Mayfield: The running game has been excellent, and being the first team to win a game without completing a pass in 52 years is a cool accomplishment, but Tampa didn't give Mayfield $55 million per year to just hand the ball off.

Even though the Bucs didn't need him on Sunday, they will need much more from Mayfield than they have gotten from him all season.

It's safe to assume Tampa will need some semblance of a passing game next week when they go on the road to face the Chicago Bears on Sunday night.

articles.title: Texans vs. Chargers Opening Odds: Bolts face another test in Week 9
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are turning the page to their next game against the Houston Texans.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-7 after falling to the Los Angeles Rams on the road in Week 8. Now the Chargers will have a chance to face off against the Houston Texans at home in Week 9.

The Texans have found their fair share of struggles this season at 2-5, but they are fresh off of their annual bye and are well-rested for the matchup. The Bolts entered this week as 4.5-point underdogs, per FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under is currently set at 41.5 points.

The Chargers struggled once again when facing the Rams. The Chargers had a 9-3 lead with 2 minutes to go in the second quarter, but they proceeded to give up a touchdown drive to close out the first half, which gave the Rams the lead going into the locker room. From there, the Rams capitalized and scored twice more in the third quarter to take a 24-9 lead, which ended up being the final score.

Hope is not lost for the Chargers as they hold on to the No. 1 overall pick for the 2027 NFL Draft. However, getting a win or two would give them some morale for the second half of the season.

Perhaps this will be the week the Chargers will have a chance to get their first win.

BFTB community, how do you feel about the Chargers possibly getting their first win of the season against the Texans at SoFi Stadium in Week 9? Let us know in the comments section below.

articles.title: Broncos’ Bo Nix left nearly speechless by ‘magical’ home after besting Chiefs
articles.summary: Bo Nix expressed amazement toward the atmosphere of the home crowd following the Denver Broncos’ remarkable win over the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday evening...
articles.body:
Bo Nix expressed amazement toward the atmosphere of the home crowd following the Denver Broncos' remarkable win over the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday evening.

Nix is halfway through the third season of his budding NFL career. He achieved significant success last season, leading Denver to the AFC Championship game before going down with a foot injury. He looks to pick up where he left off, having serious aspirations of getting his squad to the Super Bowl.

They got off to a slow start, but they have since put together a solid stretch of wins to assert themselves in the playoff race. Beating the Chiefs added a valuable win to their resume, showing off their status as serious playoff contenders. Nix reflected on the comeback after the game, thanking the fans for staying and giving the team all their support.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Something's magical about this place. I don't know. I can't explain it," Nix said on the CBS broadcast.

How Bo Nix, Broncos played against Chiefs

Bo Nix and the Broncos dug deep to pull off the comeback against Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. Denver fans are certainly thankful for it, getting to see their team take down one of the best squads in the NFL.

Kansas City boasted the upper hand for most of the matchup, taking 24-13 lead going into the fourth quarter. Denver came alive in the last 15 minutes of regulation, scoring the last 15 points of the memorable contest.

Nix enjoyed a solid performance leading the balanced offense. He completed 20 out of 32 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns.

Jonah Coleman was active as a rusher and pass-catcher for Denver. He racked up 11 carries for 41 yards and a touchdown while catching four passes for 63 yards. Courtland Sutton came next with four catches for 53 yards, Jaylen Waddle had three receptions for 39 yards and a touchdown, while Nate Adkins caught two passes for four yards and a touchdown.

The Broncos will look forward to their next matchup, being on the road. They take on the Carolina Panthers in Week 9 as kickoff commences on Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET.
