articles.title: Kansas City Chiefs implode against Denver Broncos, Baker Mayfield sets remarkable stat and Lamar Jackson suffers new setback - NFL Sunday Review
articles.summary: NFL Sunday Review - we reflect on a dramatic weekend in the NFL as the Denver Broncos stunned the Kansas City Chiefs late, while the Arizona Cardinals came from behind to beat the Dallas Cowboys and Joe Burrow guided the Cincinnati Bengals past the Tennessee Titans in overtime
articles.body:
Did you ever have the friend at school who did nothing in the group project? Mayfield was said friend as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers beat the Atlanta Falcons 16-0 without completing a single pass. Not one.

It was the first time since 1974 a team had won a game without completing a pass, the former No 1 pick finishing zero of three as Tampa leaned on the run in the pouring rain a week on since Mayfield threw for just 64 yards in his side's 43-14 win over the Carolina Panthers.

Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell combined for 310 rushing yards on 52 carries to sink a Falcons team marred by Michael Penix Jr's four interceptions and sorry 12.0 passer rating. It would encapsulate a bizarre Week Eight in the NFL, one of the lead stories from which came in Mile High.

Patrick Mahomes, Kenneth Walker and the Kansas City Chiefs were right there at the one-yard line, primed to shatter Broncos' hearts in the final seconds of a thriller at Empower Field. Just moments earlier Jonah Coleman had punched in a five-yard touchdown run to give Denver a 28-24 lead amid an 11-point fourth-quarter comeback.

Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph spoke earlier this week of the 'desperate' brand of football he was seeking from a porous unit under fire for its league-leading missed tackle tally. The Broncos have been a toothless shade from the ferocious defense that spearheaded their march to the No 1 seed last season, but Joseph's wishes were about to be fulfilled.

Kansas City's first play from the one-yard line was an incomplete pass. Their second saw Walker stuffed by JL Skinner for no gain. Their third, on fourth-and-goal, was a touchdown pass to Rashee Rice... until it wasn't. Right tackle Jaylon Moore was flagged for a false start on the biggest play of the game to epitomise his side's final stanza implosion, the Broncos sensing blood on the ensuing play as Patrick Mahomes was swarmed for a game-icing sack by Malcolm Roach.

According to Next Gen Stats, the Chiefs had a 76 per cent chance of winning upon reaching first-and-goal at Denver's four-yard line in the final minute, only to come up empty.

Andy Reid's side hurt themselves a drive earlier when Harrison Butker fired his 54-yard field goal attempt wide for what would have been a 27-21 advantage. And perhaps even earlier in the fourth quarter when Reid elected to punt on fourth-and-one from his own 41 rather than trusting both himself and his generational quarterback to move the chains. This was Reid, this was Mahomes. And yet somehow he forgot.

By the close the Chiefs were guilty of 11 penalties for 105 yards, none more costly than Moore's false start, while Butker departs Colorado under mounting pressure following the controversial addition of Justin Tucker. The former Ravens kicker was signed to the Chiefs' practice squad earlier in the week despite serving a 10-game suspension last season for violating the league's personal conduct policy following allegations of sexual assault. Butker is now two of seven from 50-plus yards and has missed a league-high 16 field goals since last season.

With Sunday's collapse the Chiefs squandered a golden opportunity to take ownership of the AFC West, having beaten Denver 31-10 in Week One. It would mark a second straight defeat after last weekend's blowout loss to the Seattle Seahawks, while wasting a commanding Patrick Mahomes performance that saw him go 30 of 41 for 321 yards and three touchdowns. This offense has sputtered through the last three years desperately fighting to rediscover its old spark - here it was and yet foot-shooting errors would cost them once more.

Broncos quarterback Bo Nix has been widely-criticised for his disappointing start to the season, but Sunday's result was the third time in his career he has brought Denver back from a double-digit fourth quarter deficit to win, the most since 2024. In Jonah Coleman Sean Payton may have found his coveted answer to a stagnant run game, while Denver's goalline stand was a self-reminder of their capabilities after another modest performance in the face of a ticking Chiefs attack, which unleashed its own rising backfield asset in rookie Emmett Johnson with 143 total yards on the day.

The Chiefs fall to 5-2. The Broncos take top spot in the division at 6-2. Another twist. No outright frontrunners. It's heating up as we enter the holiday season.

There is a voodoo doll that doesn't want Lamar to win. It is spooky season, and Baltimore's worst nightmares came true, not for the first time. You really couldn't write it. The Ravens had arrived at Highmark Stadium enthused by the return of their two-time MVP quarterback from a three-game absence due to a high ankle sprain, only to see Jackson suffer a game-ending thumb injury on his first play from scrimmage in Baltimore's 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills. Jackson entered Sunday having missed 17 games through injury since his first full season as starter in 2019, including four last year as the Ravens missed the playoffs. It has been a recurring, unavoidable and yet cruel hindrance to a Super Bowl contender, Baltimore an entirely different proposition without No 8 and, arguably, so too Derrick Henry. Jackson will undergo surgery on his thumb and miss at least the next four games on injured reserve, while further injury to backup Tyler Huntley leaves undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano as their only option, unless Jesse Minter dips into the trade market. The Ravens season is on the brink.

The Bengals are still impossible to trust as contenders. No matter how box office Joe Burrow is, no matter how dynamic the league's best wide receiver tandem is. Cincinnati's three-time Pro Bowler became the second quarterback in NFL history and the first in 75 years to record 450 passing yards, five passing touchdowns and a rushing touchdown as the Bengals survived to beat the Tennessee Titans 43-36 in overtime; he also threw three interceptions to Amani Hooker, had to overcome a 13-0 deficit for the second week in a row and saw his defense allow Cam Ward his first career 300-yard game alongside 117 rushing yards from Tony Pollard. It took the talents of a top-five quarterback to dig both himself and his team out of trouble; not all teams have that luxury, and it forever remains the question as to how sustainable said box office fireworks are for a prospective Super Bowl team. It would notably come down to a Bengals defensive hold to seal it in overtime, and the 5-2 Bengals remain capable of hurting every team in football. But can they be trusted? Not yet.

Darnell Washington is the scariest player in football. Seriously, what are you supposed to do with a human polar bear running towards you? Last weekend saw Paris play stage to his spectacular bully ball reach-over touchdown catch on Kool-Aid McKinstry, as if the uncle dwarfing his nephews at Thanksgiving dinner. On Sunday he cut the figure of a freight train while marauding down the sideline with ball in hand on his way to a 58-yard gain that would tee up Jaylen Warren's one-yard touchdown in Pittsburgh's 27-6 win over the Cleveland Browns. The Steelers tight end is listed at 264lbs; I'm here to tell you that is probably a lie. He looks upwards of 300, while standing at six-foot-seven as the most daunting mismatch in the NFL.

Drew Petzing: The jury has been out on the Lions offensive coordinator. A Ben Johnson-set bar will do that. But Sunday was a win for Petzing as his persistence in the running game finally broke through the Minnesota Vikings and their famed Brian Flores defense. Petzing's offense ran the ball 39 times for 230 yards and a touchdown, 153 yards of which came courtesy of Jahmyr Gibbs. The ground game was defining, but Petzing's flashpoint arrived on a third-and-eight in the third when he lined up Amon-Ra St Brown 15 yards behind the line of scrimmage before checking it down to his chief receiver, who followed two blockers to move the chains. If that is Ben Johnson, the league is losing its mind.

Kirk Cousins: The man that just refuses to go away. Kirk Cousins might be having as much fun playing Las Vegas Raiders football as he has ever had in his career. Every week you wonder if Klint Kubiak is edging closer towards Fernando Mendoza time, only for Cousins to fend him off. The veteran quarterback went 19 of 26 passing for 247 yards and three touchdowns, including a Brock Bowers beauty, to lead the Raiders to a 38-33 win over the New York Jets, lifting Las Vegas back to 4-4. He is still hanging around.

Indianapolis Colts: The Colts began the week by trading away All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, and ended it in a dismal 42-7 defeat to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Somewhere in between they also reportedly placed star running back Jonathan Taylor on the trade block. Their season is over and an ugly rebuild looms for a spiralling franchise that last month fired its General Manager in a consequence of its failure to find a long-term quarterback solution. They are 2-6 and starring down the barrel.

Christian Parker: The Cowboys entered the season with fresh hope of a defensive turnaround with which to complement their high-powered passing attack behind first-year coordinator Christian Parker. His defense, though, came into Week Eight ranked fourth worst in total yards allowed, before surrendering 467 yards on offense and blowing a 14-point fourth-quarter lead against a Cardinals team that replaced its quarterback three quarters in. Time is ticking for both Parker and head coach Brian Schottenheimer.

Player of the Weekend - Bhayshul Tuten, RB, Jacksonville Jaguars

Liam Coen's Jags offense is purring. And with balanced football comes a growing contender, the only blemishes on which are marginal defeats to the Broncos and Texans that they will feel they should have won. As Trevor Lawrence continues to play the best football of his career, the Jags are welcoming a breakout year for running back Bhayshul Tuten, who recorded 104 rushing yards and a touchdown alongside two catches for 55 yards and a score in Jacksonville's win over the Colts. In doing so he became the first Jags player ever to rush for 100-plus yards with a rushing touchdown and record 50-plus receiving yards with a touchdown catch in the same game. Shout to his teammate Rayuan Lane III, who scored a 92-yard pick-six.

How about a 79-point overtime thriller between the Bengals and Titans? Burrow accounted for six total touchdowns, including five touchdown passes in regulation and an overtime rushing score, while former No 1 pick Ward diced open Cincinnati's defense to the sight of 304 yards and two touchdowns in arguably the best game of his NFL career. A back-and-forth contest saw three lead changes and a tied score in the fourth quarter, the Bengals escaping as winners.

articles.title: NFL Week 8: The Cowboys can’t close, the Chargers can’t score, and Lamar Jackson can’t stay healthy
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys, Los Angeles Chargers and Atlanta Falcons all lost in dispiriting ways Sunday, while Tampa Bay won using a strategy not seen in 50 years.
articles.body: When Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott ran in a touchdown with more than 14 minutes left in Sunday’s fourth quarter, a quarter-century’s worth of football history suggested the game was effectively over. The score put Dallas ahead of Arizona 24-10, and since 2000, the Cowboys had never lost when they led by at least 14 points in the fourth quarter at home. Their record in such circumstances was a perfect 69-0, according to ESPN. Now it’s 69-1. As has been the case for the last two seasons, the Cowboys’ much-maligned problems defensively cost them again. This time, even though the Arizona Cardinals had benched their starting quarterback and turned to backup Gardner Minshew, Dallas allowed 20 fourth-quarter points en route to a 33-30 loss in overtime. The Cowboys were lucky to make it to overtime, too — Arizona missed a point-after kick with 6 seconds left in regulation that would have broken a 30-30 tie. It was the Cowboys’ second improbable loss of the season, following a Week 3 loss in which they led with 7 seconds to play, only to lose on a walk-off field goal after having surrendered a long pass play to set up the kick. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones was shown on the broadcast Sunday banging the tabletop in front of him after the loss. Asked about the possibility of firing coach Brian Schottenheimer amid a 3-5 start to the season, Jones told reporters afterward that “that’s not in my mind at this time” and expressed confidence in the coach. Prescott said, “It’s all of us; don’t put the blame on one person.” Schottenheimer will have more time, but how much? His background is on offense, and Dallas’ has regularly ranked among the league’s best during his tenure, yet the Cowboys gained only 3.6 yards per play Sunday, with their rushing offense gaining an anemic 2.4 yards per carry. Arizona committed two turnovers, it was just 8 of 18 on third down, and it still won. Lamar Jackson out at least four weeks Ever since Lamar Jackson became an MVP candidate early in his career in Baltimore, the Ravens have begun each season wondering whether this would be the year they would break through to a Super Bowl appearance behind their star quarterback. It has yet to happen, and this doesn’t seem to be their year, either. Playing his first game since he missed the past three with a high ankle sprain, Jackson was hit on the thumb of his throwing hand on Sunday’s first play and never returned in a 36-10 loss in Buffalo. The injury will require surgery on the thumb, and he will miss at least the next four games and was placed on injured reserve, Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. When Jackson has been injured in recent seasons, backup Tyler Huntley has often subbed in capably. Yet when Huntley left the Buffalo loss, too, because of an injury, Baltimore struggled behind its third-string option. The Ravens are just 4-4, while Buffalo improved to 6-1. The Bills have won 12 consecutive regular-season games when they have come off byes, the second-longest streak all time. Cleveland comes back to earth How real was Cleveland? The question loomed over the Browns’ 5-2 start, which, while it was unexpected, also seemed unsustainable. Deshaun Watson had led game-winning drives in either the fourth quarter or overtime in all five wins. Sunday’s game on the road against division rival Pittsburgh — whom the Browns had already beaten once — was a key litmus test. Pittsburgh won, 27-6. The Browns still very well may turn a corner this season, but they still can’t win in Pittsburgh, where they have lost 23 consecutive games, helping the Steelers tie the record for most consecutive home victories against the same opponent. Watson threw for 324 yards but was sacked eight times. Pittsburgh is now 6-2, but its next two games are on the road, where it has averaged just 17.3 points per game this season. At home, the Steelers are averaging 27.7. A most unusual win Tampa Bay coach Todd Bowles came up with the Buccaneers’ extraordinary game plan when he saw the forecast for Week 8. “We knew it was going to be nasty,” he said. With standing water on their home field and rain falling after kickoff, the Buccaneers became the first team since 1974 to win without completing a pass in their 16-0 victory over Atlanta. In a game featuring five fumbles and four interceptions, the Buccaneers were 0-3 passing but rushed for a franchise-record 324 yards to pull off the kind of win the NFL might not see for 50 more years. The Chargers can’t win or score touchdowns While Tampa Bay was using the season’s most one-dimensional offense to succeed, the Los Angeles Chargers can’t score a touchdown no matter what offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel attempts. During Sunday’s 24-9 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, their SoFi Stadium co-tenant, the Chargers remained winless (0-7) while producing another bleak offensive performance. They have now gone 27 consecutive drives without a touchdown, per ESPN’s tabulation. It’s the league’s longest touchdown dry spell since Miami did it in 2024, when McDaniel called plays for that offense, too. Los Angeles has scored nine offensive touchdowns this season, the fewest in the league by three. Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh didn’t want to address whether McDaniel was the right play-caller for the job afterward. “I’m focused on this game, we’re gonna go watch this tape, and I believe in our guys, I believe in our players, our coaches,” he said. They’re 2-4-1. Can they still make the playoffs? In most of the NFL’s divisions, a win to improve a team to 2-4-1 wouldn’t mean much for its playoff hopes. The downtrodden NFC East isn’t like most, though. Washington’s win over Philadelphia on “Sunday Night Football” gives the Commanders (2-4-1) a 25% chance to still win the division, per NBC Sports projections. The Commanders dropped Philadelphia 27-10 to send the Eagles (2-6) to their worst start since 1999 and their first six-game losing streak since 2012. The Eagles’ playoff hopes are nearly dead, but everyone else’s in the division are still in play, even though Dallas (3-5) and Washington have endured brutal starts to the season. Division-leading New York (4-2-1) still has to play the Cowboys and the Commanders once each.

articles.title: Report Card Grades for Browns' NFL Week 8 Game vs. Steelers
articles.summary: Ugly. That's the one-word report card for the entirety of the Cleveland Browns performance in a 27-6 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.body:
Ugly. That's the one-word report card for the entirety of the Cleveland Browns performance in a 27-6 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers.

The blowout loss moves the Browns' record to 5-3 on the season and knocks them out of first place in the division. Perhaps more than that, it showcased some of the shortcomings that have been hidden behind a series of close wins for the team this season.

The offensive line issues, lack of run game and run defense all played a role in a lopsided loss.

Let's get a little more granular with those grades to diagnose who played well and who came up short in the disappointing loss.

Deshaun Watson's afternoon exemplified the idea that the final statline can lie.

The quarterback connected on 27 of his 39 pass attempts and threw for over 300 yards for the second week in a row. He had no interceptions. In a vacuum, that looks like a pretty good day at the office.

The Browns managed just nine yards in the first quarter. Watson missed a few easy throws in the first frame that would have given the offense more early momentum.

The eight sacks will mostly be charged to the offensive line, but Watson also held on to the ball longer than he needed to. He has extended plays for much of this season, but didn't do it much against Pittsburgh.

The biggest difference in this game was the ground game and some of that falls at the feet of Quinshon Judkins. As usual, the offensive line bears some of the responsibility for the blocking.

However, PFF credited Judkins with 21 yards after contact and just five yards before contact. That's abysmal on 11 carries.

Sampson didn't help the run game much either, but he did tie Judkins' best run of the game with a seven-yard gain on his only carry. His best contribution came as the team's second-leading receiver with 62 yards on six receptions.

KC Concepcion has been the high-volume target who gets the passing game going throughout the season. That didn't happen this time.

It's hard to hold Concepcion too accountable, though. The only target he didn't catch was a ball that Watson sailed over his head.

The Browns funneled 11 targets to Boston on the afternoon, putting a lot of the passing game on his plate. Boston responded with six receptions for just 37 yards. His game would have been much better if he had gotten a second foot in on a near touchdown.

Jeudy has come up with a few clutch catches over the last few weeks, but was nowhere to be found on Sunday. He had just one target and didn't haul it in. This wasn't the week to disappear.

Steelers 1st in AFC North After Beating Browns

Much like Watson, the final statline doesn't completely capture the performance from Fannin. He had a costly fumble on the first drive that set the tone for the offense.

That being said, he also put up the best performance of anyone on the offense with 10 receptions for 154 yards. He again proved to be a yards-after-the catch menace with multiple instances of running over Steelers defenders for additional yards.

Whiteheart's blocking did not help establish a run game, but he at least brought in his lone target on the day for nine yards.

This was not the rookie's finest moment. He got overextended and was pulled down by Nick Herbig on a sack, and was later beaten around the edge with speed by Alex Highsmith, which forced him to hold.

Add in the Browns' struggle to get the run game going behind him and this was a lesson learned for Fano.

Johnson gave up a hustle sack to Cam Heyward. That's understandable. The sack he gave up because he straight-up lost a rep to Kevin Jobity Jr. is a little harder to forgive.

Jenkins wasn't directly involved in a lot of the sacks, but he conceded a lot of ground in pass protection. He didn't generate much push in the pass game with Keeanu Benton across from him much of the afternoon.

Barber was called for a hold on a first-down run and his run blocking wasn't stellar to begin with. He ceded a few pressures in pass protection, but he did avoid any atrocious reps there.

Howard was probably the cleanest in pass protection all day. However, he didn't help the anemic run game and he was called for two penalties.

The first was likely on Shedeur Sanders. He held onto the ball too long on the screen and Howard was called for illegal man downfield. The second, a false start, has been a recurring issue for Howard all season.

Verse drew a lot of attention for his pregame talk. Unfortunately, he didn't live up to it. He didn't record a single sack and his lone pressure came on a screen in which he went unblocked and didn't get Rodgers down before he threw the pass.

His usual solid run defense wasn't a factor as the Steelers ran all over the Browns' front. He had just one assisted tackle the whole afternoon.

The Steelers shut down Verse and McGuire wasn't there to pick up the slack. He finished the game with just two tackles and didn't affect the quarterback all afternoon.

Williams gets a slightly higher grade just because he didn't get as big of an opportunity as Verse and McGuire. Williams had 22 snaps and managed to have three tackles.

Graham's performance was hit or miss. On one hand, he was one of few defenders who made any splash plays. On the other, he got mauled on one of Warren's biggest gains and was on skates for his 51-yard run later in the game.

Huntington registered the only sack of the afternoon. That's good. Unfortunately, that impact was outweighed by the fact that the Steelers targeted him on the trap plays that led to big runs.

The most notable was Warren's 51-yard run. Huntington got his shoulders turned and he took on the kickout with his chest instead of spilling or squeezing it.

A missed tackle and the overall lack of fits in the run game are too much for Hall's four tackles to overcome. He gets a passing grade, but it was nothing to get excited about.

Collins was the most consistent of the interior defensive linemen. That being said, none of them graded out that well given the success the Steelers had on the ground.

He had four tackles with one for a loss despite leaving the game for a while with an elbow injury.

This was an uncharacteristically bad game for the Browns star. He was not downhill against the run game for most of the afternoon.

However, it was his deficiencies in coverage that cost Cleveland the most. He was beaten by Darnell Washington in man coverage on more than one occasion, including a 58-yard reception.

Despite the rough performance from the defense as a whole, Quincy Williams was one of the few who played well. He had a tackle for loss and got his hand on a pass.

He did have a missed tackle and only added five tackles to his total for the year. It wasn't a perfect performance, but it should have been enough for the Browns to have a better result.

The Steelers ran for 200 yards, but the defense didn't really give up a lot to Rodgers and the passing game. Ward was a big reason for that and he had an interception.

It should also be noted that he attempted to tackle Rico Dowdle too high and the running back ran through him to score the first touchdown.

This was one of Campbell's best games. He gave up nearly nothing in coverage and was not an issue as a tackler either. Almost all of the Steelers' success in the pass game was to their tight ends and slot receivers.

Campbell and Ward were able to hold the Steelers' outside receivers in check. Harden had a harder time keeping up with their inside threats. He gave up a few catches in coverage and wasn't an impact player against the run.

Still, he didn't have enough major mistakes to get lower than a C.

Delpit gave the Browns' defense some juice in the first quarter when he obliterated a screen for a three-yard loss. He didn't have any major mistakes in pass coverage either.

Hickman was second on the team in tackles with seven. That wasn't a good thing. Many of those tackles happened too far downfield for the Browns to have success, but that's not really his fault.

The rookie was busy on Sunday with nine total tackles. He was one of the few bright spots for the Browns in this game. He continues to make the most of his increasing role as he did all of that with just 31 snaps.

The kicker did his part. He knocked both field goal attempts through to score all six of the team's points.

Four punts. Three were downed inside the 20 and he averaged 49.8 yards per punt. That's a good day.

articles.title: Jerry Jones says Cowboys coach won't be fired after loss but Indy's Shane Steichen has no such pledge Monday
articles.summary: Jerry Jones says Brian Schottenheimer remains the Cowboys coach while the Colts continue to quit on season, suggesting Shane Steichen's eventual ouster
articles.body: The painful but seemingly inexorable march toward head coach unemployment took another significant step in the careers of Brian Schottenheimer and Shane Steichen on Sunday. Both coaches are headed to similar dismissals which are deserved and the only reason it hasn't happened already is because the owners of the Indianapolis Colts and Dallas Cowboys are eccentric and perhaps arrogant enough to believe what is an obvious lost cause can still be redeemed. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said after Sunday's come-from-in-front overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals that Schottenheimer remains the Cowboys' coach and firing him is not a looming move. MIKE TOMLIN'S COACH CRITICISM MAKES HIM BETTER TV ANALYST BUT RAISES QUESTION WHETHER HE'S EYEING COWBOYS JOB "We're not going to get into anything, that's not in my mind at this time," Jones told the usual gaggle of reporters he entertains after home games. "The main thing that's in my mind is we tee it up for those kind of spots to win it. We really do want those situations. Call for it. Bring it on." The Cowboys got the situations they wanted, leading 14-3 at halftime and 17-10 after three quarters against the Cards. And they blew the game. The upstart Cardinals rallied behind Gardner Minshew throwing to Michael Wilson or handing it to Tyler Allgeier, who rushed for 147 yards against Dallas after gaining 64 yards the previous three games. Jones saw his team lose at home for the third time in four games. COWBOYS COACH BRIAN SCHOTTENHEIMER DEFENDS PLAYERS-ONLY MEETING DESPITE MIKE TOMLIN'S CRITICISM He saw his team fail to string together consecutive wins for the third time this season. Indeed, winning streaks are foreign to the Cowboys under Schottenheimer, because they have won consecutive games only once in his tenure. And out of all this, after losing to a roster that is less talented and slightly less experienced, Jones blamed practically everyone except Schottenheimer. "A lot of people let Brian down today," Jones said. "And so for whatever criticism we want to have of Brian, we can all get in line. To use a cliché, that was a total team effort out there for us. And we have to be, for our fans, we have to be better than that when we got our hands on a win and then drop the ball." So, Jones is staying the course for now. But that doesn't answer the fundamental question why? JONATHAN TAYLOR'S WIFE KNOWS THINGS SO DIRE FAMILY IS ON 'COLTS TRANSACTION WATCH' EXPECTING TRADES OR FIRING COLTS TRADE PRO BOWL GUARD QUENTON NELSON TO SEAHAWKS, THE FIRST OF WHAT COULD BE MULTIPLE DEADLINE MOVES The Colts were similarly trying to find answers to their continued problems after Sunday's blowout 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Colts have lost four consecutive games, fired their general manager, traded multiple star players, are on the verge of also trading running back Jonathan Taylor, and Steichen was somehow searching for reasons he's got problems. "I'm going to evaluate everything, every position going forward," Steichen said at one point when someone asked if Daniel Jones would remain his starting quarterback. Earth to Steichen: Where was this evaluation of Jones before you and deposed GM Chris Ballard agreed to give the quarterback a two-year extension in March? The coach who was all in on Jones in the offseason seemed suddenly willing to get out on Sunday. And that seems to be the prevailing culture in Indy. Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon has quit on the season by firing the GM, and ordering the systematic trading of top talent to the highest draft choice bidder. Steichen has been seemingly picked up on that and turned on Jones. And some players are turning on the season as seen by them letting the Jaguars tear through weak tackle attempts to the tune of 183 rushing yards and three passing TDs by Trevor Lawrence. Because of all this, it would not really surprise if Irsay-Gordon soon turns her quitting on Steichen. As early as Monday. With the coach's ouster. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. articles.title: $202 million losses put Travis Kelce's Six Flags investment at risk as JANA Partners demands sale talks
articles.summary: Last month, Travis Kelce's investment in Six Flags appeared to offer the NFL star an opportunity to turn his childhood memories into a successful business
articles.body: Last month, Travis Kelce's investment in Six Flags appeared to offer the NFL star an opportunity to turn his childhood memories into a successful business venture. Now, that investment is facing an uncertain future. The amusement park operator is struggling financially, and an influential group of investors is pushing for a major change in ownership. With losses mounting and its stock price under pressure, Six Flags could be heading towards a sale. The latest development has also put Kelce's business interests under fresh scrutiny, raising questions about whether the company's promised turnaround can still happen.Travis Kelce's Six Flags investment faces fresh pressure as losses mountThe growing concerns centre on activist investment firm JANA Partners, which wants Six Flags to take a serious look at potential buyers. According to the Wall Street Journal, JANA has urged the company's board to bring in an investment bank and explore a possible sale.The demand follows another disappointing financial report. Six Flags reported a net loss of more than $202 million, adding to concerns about its ability to recover from recent business setbacks.JANA, which joined Kelce and other investors in acquiring an approximately 9% economic interest in the company in 2025, has been pushing for major changes for months. Its earlier campaign called for discussions with interested buyers and a shake-up in the company's leadership."It is now in the best interest of shareholders for the company to reverse course and engage with known buyer interest in Six Flags," JANA Managing Partner Scott Ostfeld wrote at the time.The investment firm also raised concerns about the board's decisions, describing an "an alarming pattern of board dysfunction and disjointed decision-making that has become impossible to ignore."Although Richard Haddrill has since replaced Marilyn Spiegel as executive chairman, the leadership change has not eased all investor concerns. JANA's latest reported move suggests that selling the business may now be a more attractive option than continuing with its current recovery plans.Six Flags stock struggles despite Travis Kelce's backingKelce joined the investment group in October 2025 alongside former Gap CEO Glenn Murphy and technology executive Dave Habiger. The group hoped to improve the parks through better operations, stronger marketing and an improved guest experience.For the Kansas City Chiefs tight end, the deal was more than another business opportunity. Six Flags had been part of his childhood, making the investment particularly meaningful."I am a lifelong Six Flags fan and grew up going to these parks with my family and friends," Kelce said when the investment was announced. "The chance to help make Six Flags special for the next generation is one I couldn't pass up."However, the financial picture remains difficult. Six Flags shares closed at $10.88 on October 1, close to their 52-week low. The company had previously seen its stock jump nearly 20% after JANA revealed its investment, but that excitement did not last.Six Flags is also preparing to move its corporate headquarters from North Carolina to Texas in early 2027. Despite the uncertainty, the company says it remains focused on its strategic priorities and maximising shareholder value.Whether Kelce and his fellow investors can revive the amusement park business or eventually support a sale remains a major question.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Saquon Barkley Addresses NFL Trade Rumors and Eagles Future in New Video After Loss to Commanders
articles.summary: Despite the Philadelphia Eagles suffering their sixth straight loss on Sunday against the Washington Commanders, star running back Saquon Barkley made it clear that he wants to stay put.
articles.body:
Despite the Philadelphia Eagles suffering their sixth straight loss on Sunday against the Washington Commanders, star running back Saquon Barkley made it clear that he wants to stay put.

Barkley addressed his involvement in trade rumors ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline and said that he's not looking for a way out amid the Eagles' struggles.

"I would love to be here," Barkley told reporters after Philadelphia's 27-10 loss to Washington on Sunday Night Football . "I plan on being here. I don't like the way the season is going, but I am not one of those guys that wants to jump ship. That's not the type of person you want to have, and that's not the person I am. I'd rather be a part of a solution to the problem and hopefully be a reason we fix it."

Barkley registered 13 carries for 30 yards and a touchdown and added a 24-yard reception as the Eagles fell to 2-6, ranking last in the NFC East.

NFL Network's Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport reported on Sunday that the Eagles "have made it clear to teams they are not considering trading Barkley" because they "believe they have plenty of talent on the roster to compete in 2027 and beyond." However, with one game left before the trade deadline, there's still a chance that Philadelphia's plans could change.

The Eagles have been dealing with injuries to multiple key players, including star quarterback Jalen Hurts, who will miss the rest of the season. Barkley has also been hindered by back and hamstring injuries while trying to shoulder the load on offense. Despite playing through his ailments, his production has slipped, as he has just 274 yards and two touchdowns with no 100-yard games across eight weeks.

While it sounds like Barkley is currently off the table in trade scenarios, Philadelphia could look to offload some of its other top assets amid its lost 2026 season. The team's Week 9 meeting against the New York Giants (4-2-1) could determine how willing it is to sell at the trade deadline.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes' Wife Brittany Calls Out Penalty Call Overturning Chiefs' TD in Loss to Broncos
articles.summary: The wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes passionately disagreed with the false start penalty that wiped out a game-winning touchdown in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos.
articles.body:
The wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes passionately disagreed with the false start penalty that wiped out a game-winning touchdown in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos.

Brittany Mahomes said in an Instagram Story the flag "was the weakest call I have ever seen."

Patrick Mahomes hit wide receiver Rashee Rice for the go-ahead score, but the play was whistled dead before the snap. The six-time Pro Bowler questioned whether the movement by right tackle Jaylon Moore was enough to warrant the penalty.

"It didn't surprise me or catch me, so it couldn't have been big," Mahomes told reporters . "It was called. You have to go with whatever's called. But a lot of times, in those big moments, the little stuff doesn't get called like that."

"I didn't see [a penalty]; that's one man's opinion," he said. "I saw him move his head, but I didn't see a false start."

It probably doesn't become a story if the referees don't throw a flag and the Chiefs win the game. Moore's movement wasn't all that noticeable in real time.

However, subsequent replays showed his right foot did move ever so slightly backward. By the letter of the law , that's a false start.

There's no question the penalty was consequential. Kansas City isn't in that position in the first place if it doesn't squander an 11-point lead in the fourth quarter, though.

Prior to the false start, the offense also had three shots within four yards of the goal line to get into the end zone.

The frustration from the Chiefs and their fans is understandable because a close loss to a division rival is a tough blow no matter the circumstances. But Kansas City had ample opportunity to put the contest out of reach before the final seconds.

articles.title: Updated NFL Trade Rumors, Predictions for Jonathan Taylor, Saquon Barkley, Jauan Jennings
articles.summary: The NFL trade market has already served up several stunners.
articles.body:
The NFL trade market has already served up several stunners.

And, to think, we're still nowhere near the buzzer sounding, as the 2026 trade deadline won't arrive until 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, Nov. 10.

The roster-reshuffling process could actually pick up speed from here, which sounds wild when we've already seen the Seattle Seahawks land Quenton Nelson, the San Francisco 49ers reunite with DeForest Buckner and the Chicago Bears add Jeffery Simmons.

What else might be in store? Let's round up the latest buzz and break out the crystal ball to make some educated guesses.

Reunions have apparently been front and center of the 49ers' trade thoughts, as they nearly welcomed back another player in the past week.

Per Fox Sports' Jay Glaser , the 49ers and Minnesota Vikings "had trade terms worked out for Jauan Jennings," but San Francisco wanted to personally gauge his interest over FaceTime about returning. Instead, Jennings denied them and said, "I want to stay here in Minnesota."

Jennings, who spent his first five NFL seasons in San Francisco, exited to sign a one-year contract worth up to $8 million with Minnesota this offseason. But he has struggled to find his place in this passing attack, managing just six receptions on 10 targets for 54 yards and no scores so far.

Still, he has a reason he either wants to stay with the Vikings or avoid returning to the 49ers. It would have been a fun trade-season story and perhaps a significant upgrade given San Francisco's injury issues at the position, but it doesn't sound like it'll happen.

Prediction: The 49ers trade for a receiver, but not Jennings.

An injury-riddled season could convince the Philadelphia Eagles to take a seller's mindset into the trade market. Even if they go that route, though, they aren't expected to split from star running back Saquon Barkley.

ESPN's Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport reported the Eagles "have had trade talks involving some of their players," but also "have made it clear to teams they are not considering trading Barkley."

Barkley is a 29-year-old running back with a little over $35 million left on his contract, so the trade speculation is understandable. But if Philly thinks it can turn things around sooner than later, then it probably doesn't want to part with such a significant offensive contributor.

This season might be past the point of salvaging, but better fortune on the health front and an offseason to patch holes could bring this club together fairly quickly. The Eagles should arguably still have an ear open in case someone wants to put a Godfather offer on the table, but moving Barkley for anything less than top dollar wouldn't make sense.

In case the 2-6 record and possible benching of the starting quarterback didn't give it away, the Indianapolis Colts are very much open for business. They've already sent away both Nelson and Buckner, and there are reasons to believe star running back Jonathan Taylor could be next.

And he certainly could be, though CBS Sports' Aditi Kinkhabwala relayed that the Colts "are not soliciting offers" and "are not actively seeking to move him."

Functionally, this may not reveal much of anything about Taylor's trade status. The Colts might sense some leverage lost if they're the ones out making phone calls in search of offers. If nothing else, it helps to communicate the idea that they don't feel the need to trade him.

Still, with so many unknowns impacting the long-term outlook for this franchise, it's hard to envision a 27-year-old running back (who turns 28 in January) being regarded as untouchable. Especially when a number of win-now teams could really use an upgrade at the position and might pay a premium to get one.

articles.title: Kansas City Chiefs loss to Denver Broncos will come back to haunt them as Bo Nix answers critics again
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs suffer their second straight defeat after a dramatic finish to Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos; listen to Sky Sports NFL's Neil Reynolds and Jeff Reinebold as they reflect on Week Eight in the NFL on Inside the Huddle podcast
articles.body:
Denver scored 15 unanswered points in the fourth quarter while overturning an 11-point deficit to stun the Chiefs in a 28-24 win and take top spot in the division.

It came after a magnificent goalline stand as the Broncos stopped the Chiefs on four straight plays inside the five-yard line, albeit with a stroke of fortune as Jaylon Moore's false start penalty negated a would-be game-winning touchdown catch from Rashee Rice on fourth-and-goal.

The Chiefs have now lost back-to-back games after a 5-0 start following last weekend's one-sided defeat to the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks.

"It will be one that is gonna haunt them for a long time because this was a game where they could have taken control of the division," said Sky Sports NFL 's Jeff Reinebold on Inside the Huddle. "And now they're second place in the division. They've stumbled the last couple weeks. That goal line stand was one of maybe the four most intense football plays I've watched in a long time, strung right together. And what a tackle!

"On the goalline where you've got one of the top running backs, Kenneth Walker, one on one in the hole. I mean it's man measures man. You're either gonna make the play and and live to fight another day, or he's gonna run through you and get in the end zone and score.

"If you're a Broncos fan, I can't tell you how excited and how incredible it must have felt to watch your team stop one of the best offenses in football four straight from inside the five."

Denver took the lead for the first time since their field goal on their opening drive of the game when Jonah Coleman ran in a five-yard touchdown with 1.56 to play. It saw the Broncos capitalise on a short field after Harrison Butker fired his 54-yard field goal wide on the previous possession for the Chiefs.

"You can see the frustration, you had multiple opportunities," said Sky Sports NFL 's Phoebe Schecter. "Whether it's as simple as a missed field goal or false start a yard away, those pieces of the puzzle are so frustrating to a team ideally built around great fundamentals and not beating themselves.

"You have no receiving core, you are relying on your running game and tight ends but you still have to believe when you have Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes."

It was the third time in Bo Nix's NFL career that the Broncos quarterback has pulled his side back from a double-digit fourth-quarter deficit to win, the most since 2024.

Nix has divided opinion with his performance so far in the 2026 campaign but threw for 222 yards and two touchdowns to lift Denver to 6-2, enacting revenge for their 31-10 loss to the Chief in Week One.

"He's an intense competitor. That's the thing that jumps out at me every time I watch him play," said Reinebold.

"He's got the personality, much of the same personality as his head coach. They're very intense guys. Both will lay it on the line and both are emotional and play with their play and coach with their emotions on their sleeve. I like I'm watching.

"Sean Payton is ripping the defensive coaches. He's ripping the offensive coaches. The coaches are yelling back at him. It was something. You could tell they wanted to win that game very badly.

"It felt like a playoff game in some ways because these two teams have now kind of separated from everybody else. If you're Denver, certainly anytime you can go in and beat your number one rival in the division, I wouldn't say it puts Denver in the driver's seat but certainly makes it much more comfortable in first place.

"When you look at their schedule down the stretch, you'd say right now that they would be a favourite in every single one of those contests. So it's gonna be interesting to see how they handle that. Now you have to handle expectations."

articles.title: Week 9 Waiver Wire Pickups Highlighted by Tyler Allgeier, Jonah Coleman, Adonai Mitchell
articles.summary: Fantasy football managers should be afforded a bit of relief heading into Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
Fantasy football managers should be afforded a bit of relief heading into Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season.

It's not a relax-and-let-your-guard-down kind of break, but it should be a helpful one nonetheless.

For starters, only two teams have byes in Week 9, and they aren't exactly fantasy juggernauts (Pittsburgh and Tennessee). And while the injury hits keep on coming, we're deep enough into the campaign that some of the players hurt earlier this season have either returned or are nearing their comebacks.

The real icing on the cake, though, is the fact there are legitimately exciting options available on the waiver wire (rostered in fewer than 60 percent of fantasy leagues, per FantasyPros ). That isn't always the case, but the following three possible pickups all have us excited about their immediate impact and longer outlook.

Tyler Allgeier, RB, Arizona Cardinals (53% Rostered)

The Cardinals just secured their best win of the season and lost two running backs in the process: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Bam Knight (concussion).

How is that possible? Well, Gardner Minshew II sometimes morphs into a miracle-worker, and Tyler Allgeier proved he's capable of more than just mashing in goal-line carries.

Allgeier was unstoppable on Sunday. His 11 carries yielded 147 yards and a touchdown. His five targets delivered five catches for 44 yards and another score. Heading into Monday night, he has the second-most fantasy points from Week 8 of anyone (half-PPR scoring format).

If he controls the backfield for a bit while the others deal with injuries, he could be a viable starting running back in fantasy. But the fact he warrants flex consideration even when the others are at full strength is what should make him a no-brainer addition.

Jonah Coleman, RB, Denver Broncos (57% Rostered)

Fantasy managers were advised last week already to get out and get Coleman.

Not enough of them listened. But if they don't heed the advice this time around, they won't get another opportunity to correct that mistake.

Coleman looked good in his first game back from injury last week, but he looked great on Sunday. He needed only 15 touches (11 carries, four catches on five targets) to tally 104 scrimmage yards and a score.

The Broncos may not always utilize their running backs exactly the way we'd like, but it feels like this toothpaste can't go back into the tube. Coleman looks dynamic, and Denver's offense could certainly stand to be more dynamic.

Adonai Mitchell, WR, New York Jets (11% Rostered)

Last week, Mitchell played his first game in more than a month after undergoing finger surgery. The Jets slow-played him right away, ultimately sending him just three targets and not connecting on any.

This week, though, the kid gloves came off—and the production returned almost immediately.

New York looked his way early and often, and Las Vegas never found a way to quiet his impact. By game's end, Mitchell had managed to turn nine targets into seven receptions for 142 yards and a touchdown.

This receiving room is a little crowded (Omar Cooper Jr. went silent Sunday), so there is certainly boom-or-bust to Mitchell's profile. That said, he just flashed a high enough reward to justify the risk.

After firing general manager Chris Ballard and kicking off a fire sale last week, the Indianapolis Colts reportedly have players planning their exits.

According to The Athletic's Mike Sando , the Colts' recent moves have "resonated in the Indy locker room, where multiple players are either openly or privately hoping to be sent elsewhere."

Following Ballard's firing, the Colts shipped away two of their best players, sending eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers. Sando noted that the decisions "sent a shrill signal to the world that they've given up on the 2026 season."

ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport of NFL Network also reported on Saturday that the Colts "are now open to trading" star running back Jonathan Taylor. The list of interested teams reportedly includes the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings and New York Giants.

Indianapolis fell to 2-6 with Sunday's 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. To make matters worse, the team doesn't own its 2027 first-round pick after sending it to the New York Jets as part of last year's Sauce Gardner trade.

Sando noted that it appears the Colts will "continue to go through the motions for the next two-plus months" as they play out the rest of the 2026 campaign. It sounds like multiple players are hoping to be gone from the franchise before it's all said and done.

articles.title: Detroit Lions star Jack Campbell rushed to hospital after tackle leaves him motionless on field
articles.summary: Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell was rushed to the hospital after a tackle in the Minnesota Vikings game left the standout defender facedown and motionless on the Ford Field turf.
articles.body: Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell was rushed to the hospital on Sunday after a tackle left the standout defender facedown and motionless on the Ford Field turf. The serious injury cast a pall on Detroit locker room as players cut short their celebration of a dramatic 19-15 victory over division rivals the Minnesota Vikings. Coach Dan Campbell, who is not related to the star linebacker, had been jubilantly shouting out his players before shifting the postgame address to their injured teammate. “I do not have any more information on Jack,” he told players. “We don’t know anything else at this point. So here’s what I want to do: We’re going to take a knee, I want to pray for Jack. Let’s keep him in our thoughts and prayers.” On the first play of the fourth quarter, Vikings QB Kyler Murray connected with T.J. Hockenson for a 10-yard gain with Campbell and teammate Eric O’Neill bringing down the Minnesota tight end in what appeared to be a routine tackle. But Campbell became immediately prone, face down and not moving as medical staff rushed on to the field. The linebacker was strapped into a medical cart and driven away. Campbell showed proper form, with his head up, in making this by-the-book tackle. But it appeared Campbell’s head and neck might have been forced backward as his helmet made contact with Hockenson’s left hip. “Jack Campbell is resting and will remain in a local hospital tonight, for continued evaluation and monitoring,” the Lions posted to social media on Sunday after the game. “The team will provide further updates as we have them.”
